Name: Russian silver chalice
Description: Chalice with the representation of the Deesis in medallions.
Icon with the Resurrection of Jesus Christ and Descent to the Hell surrounded by representations from the cycle of the Twelve Great Feasts.

Name: Triptych in the Holy kalyve of Timios Stavros
Description: Περίτεχνα τρίπτυχα με ανάγλυφες παραστάσεις (ρωσικά και ρωσικής τεχνοτροπίας)

Name: Censer in the Holy kalyve of Timios Starvros
Description: Θυμιατό ασημένιο, ρωσικής τεχνοτροπίας

Name: Icon with Saint Nicholas in the Holy kalyve of Timios Stavros
Description: Εικόνα του Αγίου Νικολάου, ρωσικής τεχνοτροπίας (κειμηλιακό έργο)

Name: Chalice in the Holy kalyve of Timios Stavros
Description: Αγιον Ποτήριον, ρωσικής τεχνοτροπίας

Name: Micrography in the Holy kalyve of Timios Stavros
Description: The Russian Polytechnic School of Fine Arts in Saint Petersburg sent as a gift an icon of high quality representing the Birth of Christ, in order to thank the Ananaion Brotherhood for the excellent collaboration with the monastery of Saint Panteleimon.

Name: Icon with Saint Eleftherios offered to Venizelos
Description: Special technique - tsokaniko.

Name: Revetment of Saint George's icon in Zografou Monastery
Description: The icon is covered with a silver revetment that allows to see only the painted face of the saint. The revetment was fabricated in Saint Petersburg in 1837 with the benediction of the bishop of Novgorod Serapheim and with the money of the archimandritis Anatolios. It is decorated with red, green and rose precious stones on the halo, the crown and the cloths of the saint, as well as many ex-voto. The framework has a plant decoration, and on the right and on the left, in medals of elliptical form, scenes from the saint's life are represented.

Name: Gospel of the Greek community of Kallipoli with Russian gilt silver cover
Description: Gospel printed in Venice with a Russian gilded silver cover depicting the Resurrection on the front and the Descent from the Cross on the back.

Name: Icon of the Virgin Kazanskaya in Agias Triados Monastery
Description: The icon represents the Virgin facing her baby Son, who is rendered standing and blessing. The inscriptions are in Russian and the icon has many damages. The icon underwent  restoration in 2011. According to the Monastery's site, four silver coins are attached to it as offerings, "one dating from the Ottoman period with Arabic characters, one from 1673, one from 1705 and one from 1811. It also has a Mexican cross."

Name: Embroidered Miter
Description: Russian embroidered miter donated by archimandrite Meletios Myriantheus to the Christian Museum of Athens (now Byzantine and Christian Museum)

Name: Christ Pantokrator
Description: Jesus Christ is presented half-figure with the open Gospel in his left hand and blessing with his right. His cloths are decorated with silver flowers.

Name: Enkolpion with the signature of Nicholas II (Vatopediou Monastery)
Description: In the sacristy of the Monastery, there is a a gold enkolpion with the signature of the tsar Nicholas II, as well as 4 gold-woven ecclesiastical garments [χρυσούφαντες ιερατικές στολές] and 3 for diacres [διακονικές]. All of these were offered by the Tsar for his Wedding day and for his Coronation day to the Higoumenos of Vatopedi, Iakovos Dimopoulos.

Name: Icon with Saints George and Demetrios on horseback
Description: Icon with two military saints on horseback. Saint George is depicted killing the dragon and Saint Demetrios slaying an enemy.

Name: The Lamentation of the Virgin Mary
Virgin Kazanskaya, with Prophet Ezekiel and Saint Martyr Euplus
Church chandelier from Moscow in Vatopedi (placed on the right side)
Triptych depicting the Hospitality of Abraham, the Last Supper, the Marriage at Cana and the Twelve Great Feasts
Description: The three scenes on the upper parts (Hospitality of Abraham, Last Supper, Marriage at Cana) are biblical prefigurements of the Holy Communion.  The main surface of the panels is decorated with twelve christological scenes. Six of the them are identified by carved inscriptions on the upper part of the silver frame, while the other six have partially preserved painted inscriptions.

Name: Archangel Michael the Commander of the Fearsome Host
Icon with the Resurrection and Feasts
Description:
The icon has a coplex iconographical subject, the Descent into Hell with the Resurrection and feasts, inspired by the apocryphal Gospel of Nicodemus and other apocryphal texts.
The decoration consists of a central part in which the Descent and the Resurrection are conjoined, together with scenes of the Passion and Christ's appearances after the Resurrection. It is surrounded by separate spaces, depicting scenes from the Twelve Great Feasts and other feasts.

Name: Revetment of Saint George's icon in Zografou Monastery II
Description: The icon of Saint George from Arabia is covered with a silver revetment that allows to see only the painted face of the saint.

Name: Icon with St. John the Theologian
Bronze icon with the Crucifixion and the Presentation at the Temple
Description: Bronze cruciform icon with a depiction of the Crucified Jesus Christ in the center surrounded by Cyrillic inscriptions. The icon is partially destroyed, so, the right part of the icon is missing. On the left part of the Crucifix, the Virgin Mary stands accompanied be another woman. On the upper left corner there is the depiction of Presentation of Jesus Christ to the Temple.

Name: Saint George icon
Description: Icon with St George on horseback slaying the dragon against a rocky background.

Name: Two triptych panels with the Virgin and John the Baptist
Description: The two panels show the Virgin and John the Baptist praying, constituting a Deesis. The compositions are simple and only a few colors are used (red, brown and yellow ochre, black).

Name: Icon with Saint George with the Dragon
Description:
Icon depicting St. George riding on a white horse and killing the dragon against a rocky landscape.
In the past, the frame of the icon had been covered with metal oklad.
Icon depicting the Nativity of Theotokos in the centre of a rocky landscape.  In the past, the icon had been covered with metal oklad.

Name: Russian silver paten
Description: Paten with representation of Melismos.

Name: Cast bronze triptych with the Virgin and Saints
Description: The central panel depicts the Virgin blessing a crowd with a sword in the right hand, flanked by two angels. Above her, on a small rectangular panel, is a bust of the Pantocrator. Each of the side panels is separated into three rectangular registers. In each register two saints are represented, i.e. six saints on each side panel of the triptych.

Name: Brass diptych with the Virgin and Saints
Description: On the outer surface of the diptych  i.e. when closed, on the front side, the Cross on top of Golgotha hill is depicted with the skull of Adam under it and the symbols of the Passion flanking it. On the back side there is a rosette. When open, the veneration of the icon of the Virgin Kazanskaya is represented on the left side and St. Nicholas (?) on the right, flanked by two saints. Originally, the inside was probably decorated with enamel.

Name: Bronze diptych with the Last Judgement and "In thee Rejoiceth"
Description: The hymn "In thee Rejoiceth" is depicted on the left panel and the Last Judgement on the right one.

Name: Brass triptych with a Deesis
Description: Brass triptych depicting the Golgotha Cross on the outside and a Deesis on the inside.

Name: Brass diptych with the lives of Christ and the Virgin
Description:
On the outer surface (i.e. when the diptych is closed), a Cross with the instruments of the Passion are depicted inside a large central oval-shaped space. 
When open, five scenes can be seen on each side of the diptych: four on the rectangular part of the panel and one in each of the two arches. On the left one there are scenes from the life of Christ, and on the right one there are scenes of the veneration of icons with the Virgin .

Name: Bronze diptych with the Virgin and Saints
Description: The arch contains a scene with the Virgin amid saints and prophets; on the main surface are four scenes of the veneration of the icons of the Virgin.

Name: Icon with Christ Pantokrator
Description: Christ as Pantokrator is represented half length and frontally with right hand raised in a blessing gesture and left hand holding a gospel book.

Name: Icon with the Annunciation
Description: Icon depicting the announcement by the Archangel Gabriel to the Blessed Virgin Mary that she would soon give birth to the Son of God.

Name: Brass icon with the Three Hierarchs
Description: Cast brass icon with relief depiction of the Three Holy Hierarchs, in blue enamel background with flowers. The top of the composition of decorated with a composite flame-shaped arch with Jesus Christ blessing.

Name: Icon with Saint Nicholas
Description: Icon depicting Saint Nicholas of Myra and Christ with the Virgin Mary in medallions.

Name: Brass icon with the Virgin "Joy to All who Suffer"
Description: Brass miniature icon depicting the Russian iconographic subject of the Virgin "Joy to All who Suffer".

Name: Icon with the Annunciation
Description: The icon depicts the Annunciation of the Virgin following the traditional iconography of the subject in Eastern Orthodox iconography. The archangel Gabriel is shown coming in from the left, Mary stands to the right and the event is set in front of two high buildings.

Name: Icon with Saint Nicholas
Description: Icon depicting Saint Nicholas of Myra with an opened Gospel book. In the past, the icon had been covered with a metal revetment (oklad).

Name: Brass and enamel cross depicting the Crucifixion
Description: Cruciform brass icon with the Crucifixion and two side panels. At the top, the "not made by hands" image of Christ is depicted, whereas at the side panels Martha and the Virgin are shown on the left and Saint John and Centurion Longinos on the right. On the back it is decorated with floral and geometric patterns.

Name: Tetraptych with the Crucifixion, the Virgin and saints
Description: On the outside the object has two engraved scenes, the crucifixion on the front, and the Virgin with Child on the back. On the inside, on the two central panels, the Crucifixion and the Virgin are depicted again in egg tempera, corresponding to the themes of the outer surface. The saints Sophronius and Spyridon are depicted on the right panel; the left panel is lost.

Name: Icon with Saint Barbara
Description: Icon depicting Saint Barbara with the Mandylion on the top left corner. Her head is crowned with a crown is made out of silver. The style of the icon is vernacular baroque.

Name: Saint Spyridon
Description: Icon depicting Saint Spyridon in frontal pose, blessing and wearing a silver crown.

Name: Icon with the Great Deesis
Description: This is a "week" (sedmitsa) icon depicting the Deesis with Archangels, Apostles and Saints. The Russian inscriptions have been partially painted over in Greek.

Name: Dormition of the Virgin
Description: The Dormition of the Virgin is depicted on the center. The scene is surrounded by a painted frame with floral motifs and vines on a gold background.

Name: Saint Nicholas
Description: Icon with St. Nicholas flanked by the miniature half-figures of Christ and Virgin Mary in medallions.

Name: Two panels from a triptych depicting the Theotokos Vlachernitissa and the saints Demetrios and George
Description:
The triptych was crowned by onion-shaped arches. The representations inside the arches constituted a Deesis: Virgin Mary occupies the left arch, holding an open scroll and turning towards the Pantokrator who appears emerging from a cloud, blessing with both hands in the central arch.
In the central panel, against a golden background, the Virgin of the Sign (Znamenie or Vlachernitissa) is depicted, having the blessing Christ child in a medallion upon her chest. She is flanked by two Cherubim. 
On the left panel, the combination of the miracles of Saint George killing the dragon and Saint Demetrius slaying Tsar Kalojan is depicted. The two military saints are shown killing their enemies on horseback, while being crowned by two angels.

Name: Ecclesiastical veil (aeras) in Apodoulou village, Crete

Description: Icon depicting the saints George and Demetrios facing each other, wearing military uniforms and riding on different coloured horses. In the past, the icon had been covered with metal oklad (revetment).

Name: Icon with Saint Paraskeva
Description: Icon presenting Saint Paraskeva of Iconium (also known as Paraskeva "Pyatnitsa"). The saint is depicted full-length, standing frontally and holding a cross and a scroll against an ochre-colored background.

Name: Icon with the Apostles Peter and Paul and Saints Cosmas and Damian
Description: Icon representing the Apostles Peter and Paul and the Saints Cosmas and Damian frontally and full-length with Christ blessing them at the top centre of the icon.
This representation of the Virgin Mary holding the Christ child follows the iconographic type of the Kykkotissa.
This iconographic type of the Virgin Mary and Christ Child is known in Russia as the Mother of God Smolenskaya. In the past, the icon had been covered with a metal (?) revetment.

Name: Icon with the Beheading of John the Baptist and the Virgin
Description: The decoration on the front of the panel is divided into five separate registers: in the center, there is a small rectangular space with the Beheading of John the Baptist; the rest of the panel is divided into four separate rectangular spaces with depictions of the Virgin: on the top are the Virgin Kazanskaya on the left and the Virgin in the Three-handed type on the right. Below them are the scenes of the Protection of the Theotokos on the left and the Virgin "Pribavlenie Uma" on the right.

Name: Cosmas and Damian
Description: Icon depicting the Holy Unmercenaries in front of a building.

Name: Saints Constantine and Helen
Description: Icon depicring the saints Constantine and Helen with the Pantocrator above them.

Name: Russian chalice set in parish of Margarites village in Crete
Description: The chalice set consists of a silver plated chalice and  paten. They both bear incised decorations and inscriptions in the Russian language.

Name: Icon with the Resurrection and twelve feasts
Description:
The icon has a complex iconographical subject, the Descent into Hell with the Resurrection and feasts, inspired by the apocryphal Gospel of Nicodemus and other apocryphal texts.
The decoration consists of a central part in which the Descent and the Resurrection are conjoined, together with scenes of the Passion and Christ's appearances after the Resurrection. It is surrounded by twelve separate rectangular spaces, depicting scenes from the Twelve Great Feasts and other feasts.
The composition is surrounded by a painted border, with geometric ornament and panels containing identifying inscriptions corresponding to each scene. In the corners are portraits of the four Evangelists.
Icon depicting the Resurrection of Christ in the form of descent into Hell.
Icon depicting the baptism of Jesus Christ by Saint John the Baptist in the river Jordan.  In the past the frame of the icon had been covered with a metal revetment (oklad).

This representation of the Virgin with the infant Christ follows the iconographic type of the Mother of God Vladimirskaya. The Virgin is represented half-length, holding the Christ Child in her arms and slightly turning towards him.

Name: Icon with Saint Demetrios
Description: This icon depicting Saint Demetrios on horseback killing the Tsar Kalojan. In the past, the frame of the icon had been covered with metal oklad.
Encased triptych with a Deesis.

Icon in three registers with the Mother of God Kazanskaya, the Resurrection of Christ and Descent into Hell and selected male and female saints. Complex iconographic repertoire with seven separate scenes.

Icon depicting Saint Nicholas of Mozhaisk full length and in a fully frontal pose, standing on a cushion with images of Christ and the Mother of God at his shoulders. In the past, the icon had been covered with metal revetment.
Icon with Resurrection and Descent to the Hell with the Twelve Great Feasts  [?]. The icon is almost completely destroyed.

Name: Icon with Saint Paraskeva
Description: Icon depicting Saint Paraskeva of Iconium (also known as Paraskeva "Pyatnitsa"), full-length and in a frontal posea holding a cross and an open scroll against an ochre-colored landscape.

Name: Icon with Saint Nicholas
Description: Icon depicting Saint Nicholas of Myra in half-length, holding an open Gospel book.

Name: Icon with Saint George and the Dragon
Description: This icon depicts Saint George as a knight on horseback slaying the dragon.

Name: Icon with the Virgin Vlachernitissa
Description: The icon depicts the Virgin Mary in the Russian iconographic type of the Virgin of the Sign (Znamenie).  The Virgin is shown praying with outstretched hands in the "orans" position, with Christ depicted in a medallion on her chest.

Name: Icon with Saint Hermolaus, Archangel Michael and St. John the Warrior
Description: Icon with Archangel Michael flanked by Saint Hermolaus and Saint John the Warrior. The Saints are depicted in standing and frontal pose. Above the Archangel's head, Jesus Christ in bust, surrounded by clouds, blesses the Saints.

Name: Icon with Saint Nicholas
Description: Icon depicting St. Nicholas, flanked by small busts of Christ and the Virgin.
Icon with Saint Savva [?]. The icon is destroyed in several places and the saint's face is partly damaged.
Unidentified composition with a female saint in prayer (Virgin Mary?).
Two triptych panels with 4 scenes: 1.Baptism of Christ, 2. Intercession of the Virgin Mary, 3. Symbolic composition, 4. The entrance of Christ into Jerusalem.
Icon depicting Saint Nicholas of Myra with opened Gospel Book.
St Nicholas is depicted as a bearded, half-length, figure, blessing with his right hand. On his left - Christ presenting to him a gospel and on his right - the Virgin offering him an 'omophorion'.

Name: Icon with Saint Demetrios
Description: Icon depicting Saint Demetrios on horseback killing the Tsar Kalojan. In the past, the icon had been covered with a metal revetment (oklad).

Name: Russian silver censer
Description: The censer is comprised of two parts which are connected with four chains that symbolize the four Evangelists and twelve small bells that symbolize the twelve Apostles. The censer has a Russian type cross on the top.
Current Location Name: Ecclesiastical Museum of the Cathedral Church of Rethymno

Description: The icon depicts the three angels who visited Abraham at the Oak of Mamre,  also known as "Old Testament Trinity".

Name: Saint Luke the Evangelist
Description: The icon depicts St. Luke the Evangelist writing his Gospel.

Name: Christ Pantokrator
Description: The icon depicts the half-length figure of Christ in the iconographic type of the “Pantocrator”.

Name: Icon with the Resurrection and Descent to the Hell and Feasts
Description: Icon depicting the Resurrection of Christ and descent to the hell with feasts. (The painting is badly damaged and the scenes are not clearly visible.)

The Virgin and the infant Christ are depicted in the russian iconographic type known as 'Vladimir' (or Vladimirskaya). The Virgin is represented half-length, holding the Christ Child in her arms and slightly turning towards him. In the past the icon had been covered with a metal revetment (oklad).

Name: Icon with Saint Paraskeva
Description: Icon depicting Saint Paraskeva of Iconium (also known as Paraskeva Pyatnitsa). The Saint is portrayed half-length with her symbolic attributes. She holds a small cross in her right hand and an open scroll in her left hand.

Icon representing the Old Testament Trinity (also called "The Hospitality of Abraham"). It depicts the three angels who visited Abraham and Sarah at the Oak of Mamre. In the past, the frame of the icon had been covered with a metal revetment (oklad).
Icon depicting the dormition of the Virgin Mary in the presence of the apostles and Jesus Christ against an architectural background.

Name: Icon depicting the hymn "In Thee Rejoiceth"
Description: This is a small carved ivory icon that represents the hymn "In Thee Rejoiceth". It is placed in a metal frame.
Icon depicting the Resurrection of Christ and the descent to the hell surrounded by festival scenes.
Icon depicting Sts. Sava and Simeon. Both saints are shown as full-length figures in front of an architectural background.
This icon depicts the Presentation of Mary in the Temple by Sts. Joachim and Ann.
Icon presenting the figures of the Apostles Peter and Paul in full-length and scenes from their lives in the background.
Icon depicting the Dormition and the bodily Αssumption of the Virgin Mary into heaven.  In the past the frame of the icon had been covered with a metal revetment (oklad).

Name: Icon with Saint Nicholas
Description: Icon of Saint Nicholas with Jesus and Virgin Mary and scenes from their lives.  In the past, the frame of the icon had been covered with metal oklad.

Portable triptych with the Deesis (Virgin Mary, Christ and St John the Forerunner) in a metal case. The upper parts of the three panels are decorated with various episodes from the life of the Virgin and Christ.

Name: Complete chalice set in Rethymno
Current Location Name: Ecclesiastical Museum of the Cathedral Church of Rethymno

Name: Russian silver chalice cup
Current Location Name: Ecclesiastical Museum of the Cathedral Church of Rethymno

Name: Russian silver paten
Current Location Name: Ecclesiastical Museum of the Cathedral Church of Rethymno

Name: Russian silver asterisk
Current Location Name: Ecclesiastical Museum of the Cathedral Church of Rethymno

Name: Silver paten cover
Current Location Name: Ecclesiastical Museum of the Cathedral Church of Rethymno

Name: Russian Gospel cover
Current Location Name: Ecclesiastical Museum of the Cathedral Church of Rethymno

Name: Russian Episcopal miter
Description: Episcopal miter decorated with embroideries, semi-precious stones and small painted images of holy figures and saints.
Current Location Name: Ecclesiastical Museum of the Cathedral Church of Rethymno

Name: Russian disk
Description: Ecclesiastical tray with a representation of the Crucifixion incised.
Current Location Name: Ecclesiastical Museum of the Cathedral Church of Rethymno

Name: Gilded jar for holy anointing oil (chrism)
Description: Gilded  jar in the form of a tower.  Its cover is topped by a cross.
Current Location Name: Ecclesiastical Museum of the Cathedral Church of Rethymno

Name: Russian Epitaphios
Description: Epitaph with the body of Christ painted on pressed paper and embroidered on red velvet.
Current Location Name: Ecclesiastical Museum of the Cathedral Church of Rethymno

Name: Icon with an Angel in Santorini
Silver censer of Prophet Elijah monastery in Roustika
Description: The censer is comprised of two parts which are connected with four chains that symbolize the four Evangelists and twelve small bells that symbolize the twelve Apostles. The censer ends in a Russian type cross.
Current Location Name: Monastery of Prophet Elijah in Roustika, Rethymno Prefecture, Crete, Greece

Name: Russian silver chalice set of Prophet Elijah Monastery in Roustika
Description: The complete chalice set is comprised of a communion cup with its cover, a paten with an asterisk, a diskarion (tray), a lance and a communion spoon.
Current Location Name: Monastery of Prophet Elijah in Roustika, Rethymno Prefecture, Crete, Greece

Name: Russian chalice cup with cover of Prophet Elijah monastery, Roustika
Current Location Name: Monastery of Prophet Elijah in Roustika, Rethymno Prefecture, Crete, Greece

Name: Russian silver paten of Prophet Elijah monastery in Roustika
Current Location Name: Monastery of Prophet Elijah in Roustika, Rethymno Prefecture, Crete, Greece

Name: Russian Asterisk in Prophet Elijah monastery in Roustika
Description: The asterisk is part of a chalice set.
Current Location Name: Monastery of Prophet Elijah in Roustika, Rethymno Prefecture, Crete, Greece

Name: Russian Holy Lance in Prophet Elijah Monastery, Roustika
Description: Gilt silver and iron lance with incised decoration
Current Location Name: Monastery of Prophet Elijah in Roustika, Rethymno Prefecture, Crete, Greece

Name: Russian Communion spoon of Prophet Elijah monastery in Roustika
Description: Communion Spoon with incised decoration of the Holy Cross, Lance and Sponge on Golgotha hill.
Current Location Name: Monastery of Prophet Elijah in Roustika, Rethymno Prefecture, Crete, Greece

Name: Big Russian gospel of Prophet Elijah monastery in Roustika
Description: A large size Russian Gospel. The book cover is made of red velvet and in the center there is a stamp of a golden Cross.
Current Location Name: Monastery of Prophet Elijah in Roustika, Rethymno Prefecture, Crete, Greece

Name: Silver Russian Gospel of Prophet Elijah monastery in Roustika
Description: A gilt gospel cover with representations of the Resurrection and the four Evangelists in the front and the Ascension of Prophet Elijah in the back.
Current Location Name: Monastery of Prophet Elijah in Roustika, Rethymno Prefecture, Crete, Greece

Name: Russian epitaphios of Prophet Elijah monastery in Roustika
Description: Golden-embroidered  Epitaphios on red velvet with the scene of lamentation around Christ's dead body.The body of Christ is the painted on metal.
Current Location Name: Monastery of Prophet Elijah in Roustika, Rethymno Prefecture, Crete, Greece

Name: Russian polos
Description: Embroidered pole for an episcopal phelonion depicting St. Nicolaos as a bishop.
Current Location Name: Monastery of Prophet Elijah in Roustika, Rethymno Prefecture, Crete, Greece

Name: Phelonion
Description: Green phelonion decorated with yellow crosses.
Current Location Name: Monastery of Prophet Elijah in Roustika, Rethymno Prefecture, Crete, Greece

Name: Chalice set in Agios Konstantinos village, Rethymno
Description: Chalice set consisting of a chalice cup, a paten with its asterisk and two trays.
Current Location Name: Church of Saint Constantine, Agios Konstantinos village, Rethymno

Name: Russian chalice cup of St. Constantine church
Description: Chalice cup with incised decoration and inscription
Current Location Name: Church of Saint Constantine, Agios Konstantinos village, Rethymno

Name: Russian Paten of Agios Konstantinos village, Rethymno
Description: Copper paten with incised decoration of Christ Emmanuel in the clouds
Current Location Name: Church of Saint Constantine, Agios Konstantinos village, Rethymno

Name: Icon with Saint Basil the Great
Description: The saint is represented to the waist, in ornamented archbishop vestments, blessing and holding an open gospel. The Holy Mandylion is depicted in the top left corner. The icon has a wide orange-red border. A metal votive offering made in Bulgaria is pasted on the blessing hand.

Name: Icon with Saint Paraskeva
Description: The saint is represented to the waist, with ornamented garments and a crown. She holds a small cross and an open scroll. Two angels place a crown on the saint's head. The icon has an orange-red border. The angels, crown and palms had metal ex-voto revetments made in Bulgaria. After the restoration of the icon, the metal objects were removed and transferred to a new base.

Name: Russian disc (tray) in Agios Konstantinos village, Rethymno
Description: Tray with incised information depicting a Russian type Cross.
Current Location Name: Church of Saint Constantine, Agios Konstantinos village, Rethymno

Name: Complete liturgical vestment from Russia in Makrinitsa
Description: Complete Russian liturgical vestment (πλήρης ιερατική ρωσική στολή) from woven gold (χρυσούφαντο)

Name: Banner from Russia to Makrinitsa III
Description: Two-faced banner with the Virgin and Child and the Baptism, painted on woolen fabric and gold leaf, 20th c.

Name: Second Coming of Christ
Description: This printed icon represents the Second Coming in an unusual way (see text in Greek in SourcePassage/1061) and has insciptions in Russian and in Georgian. These inscriptions reveal that the icon was printed in 1895, after the approval of the Archibishopric of Moscow. In the lower part of the icon, it is specified that this print was made to commemorate the death of the tsar Alexander.

Name: Romanov
Description: Cross with portraits of the members of the Romanov family: the tsar Alexander III, his wife, his son Nicholas (the futur tsar Nicholas II) and another girl (probably princess Xenia). The composition is quite damaged and because of this, it is impossible to identify the person represented on the left (for a more detailed description in Greek, see SourcePassage/1063). Icon made from 1881 to 1890, with Russian inscriptions. It is in Dionysiou Monastery.

Name: St Mitrofan, bishop of Voronezh, the miracle-working
Description: Icon of St Mitrofan of Voronezh, the miracle-working. The saint ia represented to hold his episcopal crozier and to give his benediction (for a more detailed description in Greek, see SourcePassage/1052). Icon that could be dated from 1800 to 1900, without inscription, in relatively good state of conservation. It is in Vatopedi Monastery.

Name: Russian disc (tray) in Agios Konstantinos village, Rethymno
Description: Paten/tray with incised decoration of the Virgin with the Child and a Russian inscription.
Current Location Name: Church of Saint Constantine, Agios Konstantinos village, Rethymno

Name: St Mitrofan of Voronezh
Description: Icon of St Mitrofan of Voronezh. The saint ia represented to hold his episcopal crozier and to give his benediction with his right hand. The Virgin Vrefokratousa is also represented in the upper corner, on the left (for a more detailed discription in Greek, see SourcePassage/1054). Icon dated from 1800 to 1920, with Russian inscription. It is in Vatopedi Monastery.

Name: St Mitrofan of Voronezh
Description: Icon very damaged, only a face of a priest (monk ?) can be seen; he has black cloths and a white scapular. The decoration is gold. Probably this is St. Mitrofan of Voronezh. A Virgin Vrefokratousa can also be distinguished in the upper corner, on the left. Icon dated between 1700 and 1900. It is in Pantokratoros Monastery.

Name: Deesis
Description: In the middle of the icon Christ is represented enthroned with an open Gospel in his left hand, while blessing with his right hand. The Virgin (weraing a purple coat) is depicted at his left side and John the Baptist at his left. Behind Christ, there are two angels. In the upper part, four saints (probably apostles) are depicted. In the lower part, two saints are shown on their knees in front of the throne : their names are not readable, but they could be Sergius of Radonezh and saint Makary Zeltovontsky (??). Russian icon made between 1700 and 1850, with inscription in Slavonic.

Name: Cover of gospel in Iviron Monastery
Description: It represents Portaïtissa.

Name: Christ Pantokrator icon in Agios Konstantinos village, Rethymno
Description: Christ Pantokrator icon with Russian inscriptions.
Current Location Name: Church of Saint Constantine, Agios Konstantinos village, Rethymno

Name: Chalice set in Agia village, Rethymno
Description: Chalice cup, paten and asterisk with incised decoration and inscriptions
Current Location Name: Church of Saint Nicholas, Agia, Crete

Name: Chalice cup of Agia village, Rethymno
Description: Chalice cup with incised decorations and inscription
Current Location Name: Church of Saint Nicholas, Agia, Crete

Name: Paten of Agia village, Rethymno
Description: Paten with incised decoration of Christ Emmanuel in the clouds with inscription on the rim.
Current Location Name: Church of Saint Nicholas, Agia, Crete

Name: Russian phelonion of Arsaniou monastery, Rethymno
Description: Phelonion

Name: Icon with the Nativity and the Flight into Egypt
Description: The icon depicts the Nativity in the center with related scenes on the four corners. Going from left to right, the upper corners are occupied with the Coming of the Magi and the angels calling the shepherds, while the lower corners depict the Adoration of the Magi and the Flight into Egypt.

Name: Mother of God Hodegetria

This is, most probably, the same reliquary mentioned by Patapios (NewspaperPeriodical/220, p.223), since the inscription is the same: "Δια συνδρομής Ιννοκεντίου μοναχού Ρώσσου έτος 1864". Name: Icon Vita of St. Mary of Egypt
Description:
Against the background of a landscape with rocks and trees are painted various episodes from the meeting of the hermit Mary of Egypt with St. Zosimus, as well as the death of the saint. In the foreground is the dead saint lying on the ground with her arms crossed. Next to it stands St. Zosimus with an unfolded scroll of text. A lion stands above the deceased. In the middle plan are three scenes: the saint finds St. Mary, who hides from him because she is naked; St. Zosimus gives St. Mary a garment; St. Mary of Egypt takes communion from St. Zosimus. At the top are St. Zosimus on his knees, St. Mary standing on a cloud; angels carry the soul of the saint to heaven, where she is greeted by Christ Almighty. The icon has a wide ocher frame on which are written long quotations from the life of St. Mary of Egypt, as well as the name of the icon. There are also inscriptions in the icon field.
The wooden base of the icon is reinforced with two profiled slats.

Name: Triptych
Description:
The triptych consists of three wooden panels ending in flame (onion) shaped arches. The painting surface is decorated with twenty-one scenes from the life of the Virgin and Christ. 
Under the arches the three main episodes of the life of the Virgin are depicted. The Presentation in the temple, the Annunciation and the Nativity of Christ. 
Beneath them, on the main painting surface of the panels the feasts of Dodecaorton are depicted: the Presentation of Christ to the Temple, the Baptism, the Raising of Lazarus, the Entry into Jerusalem, the Washing of the Feet, the Transfiguration, the Crucifixion,  the Lamentation (Pietà), the Incredulity of Thomas, the Ascension, the Pentecost and the Dormition of the Virgin.
In the lower zone, five more scenes are depicted: the Exaltation of the Holy Cross, the Synaxis of the Archangels, the Birth of the Virgin, the Beheading of John the Baptist, and six hierarchs: Basil the Great, Gregory
the Theologian, Athanasius of Alexandria, John Chrysostom, Saint Spyridon and Saint Nicholas.

Name: Virgin of the Passion
Description:
The icon depicts the Virgin holding Christ with her right hand, whose head is turned towards the upper corner of the composition, where two angels are flanking the Virgin, holding the symbols of the Passion (a vessel with vinegar and the Cross). Christ is tightly gripping the Virgin's left hand finger, a detail first seen in Italian paintings of the 13th century. The position of Crist's feet, with one turned towards the viewer, is typical for this iconographic type. The Virgin is wearing a dark red maphorion, with rich golden decoration on the borders, while Christ's himation and chiton are rendered with golden stripes. The icon's background consists of fine golden lines over a green field. On the upper corners and the sides, the scene is surrounded by clouds.
The icon follows a model popular with the Cretan painters and attributed to Andreas Ritzos.
The central composition is flanked by two unidentified saints on the border.

Name: Icon with the Virgin Mary in Burning Bush
Description:
The Virgin is depicted inside a lozenge, at the center of an octagonal star consisting of two intersecting lozenges. In her left hand she is holding Christ; in her left hand, objects connected to Old Testament prophecies can be seen: the rock with Heavenly Jerusalem, Christ as King on the walls of the city (Psalm 86.3) and the Burning Bush (Exodus 3:1-5). The Virgin wears a golden maphorion, decorated with four red discs, allegorical depictions of the three winds and the sun. Around the lozenge are angels, heavenly forces and spirits: a red Cherub above her head; below her, an archangel with a sword and a censer.  On either side spirits in the form of angels are depicted: on the left the Spirit of Fear of God and on the right an angel holding the Spirit of Temperance in his hands. The two lozenges, a red one in the color of fire and a green one, symbolize the Burning Bush, inside wich the Virgin appeares before Moses. Inside the corners of the red lozenge, the symbols of the Evangelists (Angel, Eagle, Lion, Bull) are painted with grey color. In between the star's rays are eight flower pedals, inside which are depicted archangels, angels of the powers of nature (storms, darkness, frost, ice and fire) and angels symbolizing the gifts of the Holy Spirit (Exodus 11: 2-3). All of them are praising and worshipping the Virgin.
Additionally, four Old Testament prophecies about the Incarnation of the Theotokos are depicted in the corners of the icon:
her appearance before Moses through the Burning Bush, the blooming rod of Aaron (Ar. 17:23), the prophecy of Ezekiel about the "outer gate facing east" (Ezekiel 44:1-2) and the ladder Jacob saw in his dream (Genesis 12:10-19).
Four unidentified inscriptions are placed on the icons rim.

Name: Four-part Icon with Paternitas, Mother of God Kazanskaya, Saint Nicholas of Myra, Archangel Michael the Commander of the Fearsome Host, and Saint George Slaying the Dragon
Description: Jesus is presented in the center of the icon on the Cross which is placed on the ground and surrounded by white clouds against the blue sky. On his right the Virgin is presented half-figure just like Saint John the Evangelist on his left. Above, seated on a cloud, clothed in white, stands God the Father. In the upper left corner, the Mother of God Kazanskaya is presented wearing a black maphorion, leaning her head towards her Child, who is shown wearing a blue himation and a yellow chiton. In the upper right corner Saint Nicolas is depicted half-figure wearing clothes decorated with flowers and holding a closed book in his left arm. In the lower left corner we can see the Archangel Michael on a red horse and opposite him Saint George on a white horse killing the dragon who is shown in a river or lake.

Name: Icon with the Resurrection of Lazarus

Description: The iconography on the inside consists of the Virgin with Christ, surrounded by heavenly forces and the symbols of the Evangelists on one side, and the Holy Trinity, surrounded by medallions with the Mandylion and busts of prophets on the other. On the outside, the Three Hierarchs are surrounded by busts of Saint Nicholas, Saint George, seven Russian Saints and a Cherub on one side, while the Crucifixion, surrounded by busts of the Apostles, is depicted on the other.

The three scenes on the upper parts (Hospitality of Abraham, Last Supper, Marriage at Cana) are biblical prefigurements of the Holy Communion.  The main surface of the panels is decorated with twelve christological scenes. Six of the them are identified by carved inscriptions on the upper part of the silver frame, while the other six have partially preserved painted inscriptions.

Name: Small Russian disc
Description:
On December 29, 1913, on the day of the celebration of the proclamation of the Edict of Milan on the freedom of the Christian faith by Constantine the Great, Russian Tsar Nicholas II sent a gift to the Cathedral Church in Nis as a souvenir of a precious and very beautifully artistically made and gilded church vessel.
During the occupation of Serbia in 1915 until the end of the First World War, as well as during the Second World War, all these valuables were placed in a massive chest and buried in great secrecy outside the city of Nis. 
These gifts were brought to Nis by the Russian bishop Anastasia and handed over to the church administration.

In the treasury of the church there are 3 small discs from Russia

Icon with Saint Nicholas and Hieromonk Kirill (Athos)
Description: The icon of Saint Nicholas traditionally depicts him delivering a blessing and holding a book of Gospels. All these are rendered in the typical Mt. Athos style. The entire image overlaid with a stunning multi-piece silver gilt, repoussé, chased and enameled oklad. The borders banded in cloisonné on a stippled gilt ground and with conforming champlevé enamel corner and side plaques. The border of halo in ornate enameled rosettes, the Gospels cover with translucent lavender enamel over engine turning and banded in turquoise enameled beading. Suspended from the neck of Nicholas an engraved and enameled panagia engraved with a likeness of Christ and with crown finial. The vestments of Nicholas constructed as a separate piece in high relief repoussé with extensive chasing. Hallmarked Moscow, dated 1880 and with Cyrillic maker's mark AK for Antip Kuzmichev and 84 standard.
