In two medallions above his head are Jesus Christ and the Mother of God. The central field of the icon is framed with a graphic floral ornaments. The outer frame is wide, slightly convex (coffin), colored green.
Current Location Name: National Archaeological Institute with Museum, Sofia

Name: Icon with the Three Hierarchs of the Church
Description: The three saints Gregory, Basil and John, dressed in liturgical garments, with closed gospels in their hands, are represented in full length on field. The background next to their shoulders is light, above it is a dark blue sky. In the middle over their heads is represented Christ in clouds, who blesses and holds a sphere. The frame of the icon is brown-green.
Current Location Name: National Archaeological Institute with Museum, Sofia

Name: Middle Part of Triptych
Description: In the upper part of the field are depicted: Old Testament Trinity on the left and the Dormition of Virgin on the right. At the bottom in a baroque medallion is the Resurrection of Christ. Βy the sides  of the medallion are archangel Gabriel in full length (left) and  a young saint warrior (probably Nestor) on the right. Both of them are represented on a landscape background.
Current Location Name: National Archaeological Institute with Museum, Sofia

Name: Icon with the Virgin of Kykkos with scenes and saints
Description: In the central part of the icon is presented the Mother of God with the Christ Child, a replica of the miraculous icon in the Kykkos monastery in  Cyprus. The frame of the field is gold, with baroque ornaments. There is a narrow field surrounded by the same way. In its upper part is depicted the Kykkos Monastery, in a small round medallion in front of it St. Luke paints the icon. In the bottom part of this field there is a sea, in the side parts - a  mountain-forest landscape. To the right a monk holds an icon. In front of the seascape is included a Blazon with a double-headed eagle with crowns, a scepter and a sphere. The wider outer field of the icon is divided by baroque ornaments into parts. In the four corners are the evangelists who write in a interior. In the top central part is the New Testament Trinity, on the left is the Assumption of the Mother of God, on the right - the Protecting Veil of the Mother of God. Below are the busts of St. Nicholas the Miracleworker and St. Mary of Egypt, and between them is a medallion with an inscription.
Current Location Name: National Archaeological Institute with Museum, Sofia

Name: Bell in Saint Panteleimon Monastery
Description: A huge Russian bell that weighs 13 tons, has a 2.70 m. diameter and an 8.71 m. circumference. Two monks are necessary to ring it. The bell can be heard in the whole south-west side of Mount Athos and, also, in Sithonia. It was transferred by steamboat from Russia in 1894.

Name: Icon of "Virgin Mary-Joy to All who suffer" in Galaxidi
Description: The Virgin Mary is shown here wearing a crown and holding the Christ Child. A congregation of suffering humans is gathered below her. Two angels are at her feet. One of them gives bread to the hungry people and the other one water to the thirsty people.

Name: Bell in the Royal cemetery of Tatoi
Description: Two bells were placed on a pine tree, in the Royal cementary. Both have disappeared today. On the exterior surface of the bigger one, there were inscriptions in Russian and the representations of the Virgin Mary with Child, of the Christ and of Saint Nicholas. There was a breach all over it. On the low side, there was an inscription in Russian with the date of 1895. The second bell was smaller, had an inscription in Danish and the name of King George on it, as well as the date of 1904.

Name: Icon with the Entry into Jerusalem
Icon with Jesus and the Samaritan woman
Icon with Saint Nicholas in Ermoupoli
Icon with Christ enthroned in Anelio
Description: Icon of Christ enthroned holding an open gospel book with Russian inscriptions. Behind the throne, two angels standing.

Name: Icon with Saint John the Baptist in the Church of St. Paraskevi, Anelio
Description: Saint John the Baptist is standing in a frontal pose, blessing with his right hand. He holds with the left a basin containing his head and an open scroll with a Russian inscription.

Name: Icon with Saints Agape, Chionia and Irene and Saints Adrian and Natalia of Nicomedia
Description: The five saints are represented in full length in two rows on a sky blue background. Above them in the clouds, God Sabaoth blesses with both hands. Numerous holes in the frame and on the halos of each one of the saints indicate that there were repoussé covers that have not been preserved.
Current Location Name: National Archaeological Institute with Museum, Sofia

Name: Icon with St. Constantine of Murom and his sons Mikhail and Fyodor and Saints Peter and Fevronia
Current Location Name: National Archaeological Institute with Museum, Sofia

Name: Icon with the Virgin
Description: The icon shows the Virgin Mary with Christ.

Name: Icon with Jesus Christ
Description: This icon comes from the 18th century and depicts Jesus Christ.

Name: Kursk - Root Icon of the Mother of God with saints
Description: In the icon's middle part the Virgin of the Sign is represented, surrounded by a curved plant stem with flowers and with the busts of 12 prophets: Moses, David, Solomon, Isaiah, unknown, Zephaniah, Gideon, Ezekiel, Habakkuk, Zechariah, Elijah. Above all of them, in the central upper part of the icon God Sabaoth is depicted in the clouds. On the frame, to the left and right of the central scene, four saints are represented in separate fields. On the left are St. John the Baptist and St. John the Great and on the right, St. Nicholas the Wonderworker is represented on top and the female saint Saint Paraskomi below. All, except St. John the Great, are depicted full-height.
Current Location Name: National Archaeological Institute with Museum, Sofia

Name: Icon with Saints Antony and Theodosius Pechersky
Description: In the top part of the icon is represented the Mother of God sitting in clouds, holding the Christ Child with her right hand, holding a sphere in her left. The Christ Child blesses with both hands. Under the Mother of God are Saints Anthony and Theodosius of Pechersk. Anthony is dressed as a high scholar, whereas Theodosius as a hieromonk. They are both full-length, holding scrolls of text. In the foreground is the Kiev Pechersk Lavra with its main church and caves on both sides. The icon is placed in a gilded woodcarving frame.
Current Location Name: National Archaeological Institute with Museum, Sofia

Name: Icon with Christ Pantokrator
Description: Jesus Christ is depicted to the waist, blesses with his right hand, in the left hand he holds an open gospel with a text. His chiton is yellow-orange, the himation has silver ornaments. The halo and the background are silver with engraved floral ornaments. The frame is black.
Current Location Name: National Archaeological Institute with Museum, Sofia

Name: Icon with the Virgin
Description: This icon depicts the Mother of God of Kazanskaya.

Name: Icon with the Virgin
Description: This icon originates from the 19th century and depicts the Virgin and Child.

Name: Icon with the Holy Mandylion
Description: This icon comes from the 19th century and depicts the Mandylion.

Name: View of the Russian St. Andrew's Hermitage on the Holy Mount Athos from the southwest
Description: This icon depicts the Russian hermitage of St. Andrew of the Holy Mountain.

Name: Icon with Christ Pantokrator
Description: Christ Pantokrator is depicted half figure. He blesses with his right hand and holds an open gospel with a text in his left hand. His chiton is yellow-orange, the himation is decorated with silver ornaments. The halo and the background are silver with engraved rays. The frame is wide, painted orange-red.
Current Location Name: National Archaeological Institute with Museum, Sofia

Description: This Deesis icon depicting Christ enthroned and flanked by the Virgin Mary and Saint John the Baptist.
Current Location Name: Museum of the Great Meteoron Monastery (Holy Monastery of Transfiguration of Christ), Meteora, Greece

Description: Icon depicting the Beheading of St. John the Baptist.
Current Location Name: Museum of the Great Meteoron Monastery (Holy Monastery of Transfiguration of Christ), Meteora, Greece

Description: Icon depicting Virgin Kazanskaya holding the Christ child.
Current Location Name: Museum of the Great Meteoron Monastery (Holy Monastery of Transfiguration of Christ), Meteora, Greece

Name: Icon with St John the Theologian
Description: The icon depicts Saint John the Theologian with an angel on his right shoulder, holding an open book and pointing to the writing.
Current Location Name: Museum of the Great Meteoron Monastery (Holy Monastery of Transfiguration of Christ), Meteora, Greece

Name: Icon with Christ Pantokrator
Description: This icon depicts the half-length figure of Christ as Pantocrator. He is portrayed raising his right hand in blessing and holding an opened gospel in his left.
Current Location Name: Museum of the Great Meteoron Monastery (Holy Monastery of Transfiguration of Christ), Meteora, Greece

Name: Icon with the Virgin Iverskaya
Description: The Mother of God is represented to the waist, holding in her left hand the Christ Child who blesses. They are depicted on a silver background. Silver with engraved ornaments are the halos, the Virgin's  maphorion and the chiton of Christ, whereas his himation is in ochre-yellow color. The icon has a wide red frame. The icon is a replica of the miraculous icon of Mount Athos from the monastery of Iviron - The Panagia Portaitissa.
Current Location Name: National Archaeological Institute with Museum, Sofia

Name: Icon with the Virgin Vladimirskaya
Description: The icon is a replica of the Russian miraculous icon with the Mother of God of Vladimir. The Mother of God is represented to the waist, holding in her right hand Christ Child, who embraces her. They are depicted on a silver background. The halos and the veil of the Virgin's head are engraved. The himation of Christ is dark yellow. The icon has a wide red frame.
Current Location Name: National Archaeological Institute with Museum, Sofia

Description: The icon depicts the Virgin of Kursk surrounded by holy figures.
Current Location Name: Monastery of the Holy Trinity, Meteora

Name: Icon with the Virgin of Kazansk
Description: The icon is painted according to the iconographic type of the Russian miraculous icon of the Virgin of Kazan. The shoulder-length figure of the Virgin Mary is portrayed holding the Christ child at her left. Her head is slightly inclined towards the Child who is depicted in an erect frontal pose blessing with his right hand, whilst his left is covered by the folds of his himation. The garments  and the halos of both figures are ornamented with silver leaf just as the silver background. The icon has a wide dark orange frame.
Current Location Name: National Archaeological Institute with Museum, Sofia

Name: Icon with the Virgin Kazanskaya
Description: The icon is a replica of the Russian miraculous icon of the Virgin of Kazan. The Mother of God is depicted as a bust figure, and in front of her is the Christ Child standing, and looking opposite, who blesses. The maphorion of the Virgin is golden-brown, the Christ has a dark blue chiton and a golden-brown himation too. The icon has a wide brown frame.
Current Location Name: National Archaeological Institute with Museum, Sofia

Name: Icon with the Virgin Assuage My Sorrows
Current Location Name: National Archaeological Institute with Museum, Sofia

Name: Icon with the Virgin Vladimirskaya
Description: The Mother of God is represented half Figure, holding in her right hand the Christ Child who embraces her. The clothes of both of them have silver engraved ornaments. The icon has an internal ornamented frame and a wide red frame. The icon is a replica of the Russian wonderworking icon of the Virgin of Vladimir.
Current Location Name: National Archaeological Institute with Museum, Sofia

Description: Engraving with portait of Peter I.

Name: Icon with Saint Spyridon of Trimythous
Description: The saint is presented half figure, with archbishop attire and miter, blessing and holding an open gospel with a text. His garments, the miter and the halo have engraved silver ornaments. Above the saint's right shoulder is a small round medallion with a bust of Christ holding a closed gospel. St. Spyridon is presented on a silver background, the inner field is limited by an engraved silver frame. The icon's outer frame is wide and orange-red.
Current Location Name: National Archaeological Institute with Museum, Sofia

Name: Icon with Saint Nicholas of Myra
Description: The saint is presented half figure, in archbishop attire, blessing and holding an open gospel with a text. His garment and the halo have engraved silver ornaments. On either side of the saint there are two round medallions just above his shoulders. Christ is shown in the left one holding a closed gospel and blessing and the Virgin is represented in the right, holding an epithrachelion. St. Nicholas is presented on a silver background. The icon's outer frame is wide and orange-red.
Current Location Name: National Archaeological Institute with Museum, Sofia

Description: Icon of Christ Rmmanuel depicting him as a young child in a bust-length.

Name: Icon with St. John the Forerunner
Description: The icon depicts winged and haloed Saint John the Forerunner as the Angel of the desert.

Name: Dormition of Mother of God
Description: Icon depicting the Dormition of the Virgin. The Mother of God is depicted in the center, lying on Her deathbed and flanked by the apostles, bishops and the Savior who holds the soul of the Holy Virgin Mary. There is also an architectural background.

Name: Phelonion, Gold-threaded Ottoman silk brocade (sevai)
Description: Gold phelonion decorated with gold flowers and crosses.
Triptych with three scenes: the Annunciation (left),
Triptych with three scenes: The Annunciation (left panel), The beheading of John the Baptist (central panel),

Name: Icon with the Virgin
Description: The icon depicts the Virgin Mary.

Name: Icon with Despot Djuradj Brankovic with family
Description: Serbian saints from the Branković family are depicted on the icon.

Name: Icon with St Mitrophan Bishop of Voronezh
Description: The icon, which originates from Russia, depicts the Saint Mitrophan.

Name: Saints Sava and Simeon
Description: The icon depicts the Serbian saints, Sava and Simeon.

Name: Icon with the Holy Great Martyr Paraskevi
Description: Saint Paraskevi is depicted half figure, holding a cross and an unfolded scroll with text. Her head is covered with a white veil over which there is a crown. His undergarment is orange, above it she wears a cloak, the front part of which is ornamented with an engraved silver ornament, its lining is light green. To the left of the saint, a small medallion depicts the Holy Mandilion. The background is silver and icon's frame is orange.
Current Location Name: National Archaeological Institute with Museum, Sofia

Name: Icon with Christ Pantokrator
Description: Christ is presented half figure, blessing and holding a sphere. Only his head and palms are painted. There are traces of nails around the head and on the edges of the board, which fastened the thin metal repousse cover, which now is missing. There aren't original inscriptions.
Current Location Name: National Archaeological Institute with Museum, Sofia

Name: Icon with the Virgin of the Sign
Description: The Mother of God is presented full face, raising hands, and in front of her is the Christ Child in a round medallion. Only their heads and palms are painted. There are traces of nails around the head of the Virgin and on the edges of the icon, where a thin metal repousse cover was. Only a small fragment of it is in its place.
Current Location Name: National Archaeological Institute with Museum, Sofia

Name: Icon with the Council of the Apostles
Description: The twelve apostles are represented in two groups. Their names are written on their halos. In the center app. Peter and Paul hold a model of a temple with three domes. Christ Pantocrator in clouds blessing above them. The backgroung is tricolor - green on the bottom, ocher in the middle, reddish-brown - top. The icon has a wide orange-red frame.
Current Location Name: National Archaeological Institute with Museum, Sofia

Name: Icon of the Virgin Mary in Monodendri
Current Location Name: Church of St. Athanasious, Monodendri, Epirus

Name: Icon With the Protecting Veil of the Virgin
Description: The icon field is divided into two. On the bottom left are a man and a woman with royal robes and crowns, a priest is in the center (the names of the three are illegible) and St. Deacon Roman, on the right are St. Andrew the Fool, pointing up, and St. Epiphanius. On the top of the icon against the background of a church crowned with a cross, is the Virgin Orans in a medallion, behind her - two archangels, and on the side there are groups of saints. Above the Mother of God is the medallion of Christ in clouds. They are all in clouds. The icon has a wide orange-red frame.
Current Location Name: National Archaeological Institute with Museum, Sofia

Name: Icon with the Holy Mandylion of Christ
Description: On the whole iconic field is presented a white ornamented cloth with connected upper ends, held by two angels. In its middle is the face of Jesus Christ. The background is brown. The frame of the icon is yellow.

Name: Theotokos Hodegetria
Description: Icon with the Virgin depicted in the iconographic type of the "Virgin Hodegetria".

Name: Icon with the Archangel Michael on horseback (Angel of the Apocalypse)
Description: The Archangel Michael appears as the Rider of the Apocalypse, sitting on a winged horse.

Name: Icon with Christ Pantokrator
Description: The icon is composed of chromolithograph image and metal decoration. Christ is presented to the waist, blessing and keeping the gospel closed. A repoussé of thin metal covers the body except the hands and face. The background is decorated with thin metal ornaments, but there are some missing. The icon is placed in a box, which front door with glass is missing. Family legend says that at the Epiphany the housewife carried the icon to the Old River above the town of Batak and washed it there with clean water.

Name: Icon with Saint Nicholas
Description: The icon is a chromolithograph with metal repoussé. St. Nicholas is presented to the waist, blesses and holds a closed gospel. A thin metal leaf with engraved ornaments covers the saint's body except his hands and face. The icon is placed in a box with a glass door and a lamp holder.

Name: Icon with the Virgin Mary in Prayer
Description: Icon depicting Virgin Mary praying and holding an inscribed scroll.

Name: Khorugv Resurrection of Christ - Saint Olga of Kiev
Description: On one side of the khorugv in a rectangular field is the Resurrection of Christ - the Risen Christ and a kneeling angel. On the other side is St. Princess Olga depicted to the waist. The lower part of the banner has three rounded "tails" (endings). The background is filled with painted ornaments.

Name: Icon with the Virgin Mary in Prayer
Description: This icon depicts the Virgin Mary praying and holding an inscribed scroll.

Name: Icon with the Hospitality of Abraham
Description: This icon depicts the iconographic theme of the Hospitality of Abraham, also called "Old Testament Trinity".

Name: Khorugv Resurrection of Christ - Saint Nicholas
Description: On one side of khorugv, an oval medallion with a baroque ornamented frame, is depicted the Risen Christ with a kneeling angel. On the other side in the same medallion is St. Nicholas, with Christ and the Virgin Mary in the background. On the three tails of the banner are painted the instruments of Christ's passion and church utensils. The inscriptions are in Russian, but illegible.

Name: Khorugv Baptism of Christ - Virgin Kazanskaya
Description: On one side of the khorugv, an oval medallion with a baroque ornamented frame, is depicted the Baptism of Christ. On the other side in the same medallion is a replica of the miraculous icon of the Virgin Mary of Kazan in the background. On the endings of the banner are painted the instruments of Christ's passion and church utensils. The inscriptions are in Russian, but illegible.

Name: Icon with St. Alexander Nevsky
Current Location Name: Church of the Holy Trinity in Gornji Adrovac

Name: St. Prince Lazar of Serbia
Current Location Name: Church of the Holy Trinity in Gornji Adrovac

Name: Princess Olga of Kiev
Description: The icon depicts St. Olga, in a standing position, holding a cross in her right hand and a white cloth with a church on it in her left hand. It was painted by the Serbian artist Dušan Obrenović who followed closely the iconographic prototype set by the Russian painter Viktor Vaznetsov.
Current Location Name: Church of the Holy Trinity in Gornji Adrovac

Name: St. Stephen Lazarevic
Current Location Name: Church of the Holy Trinity in Gornji Adrovac

Name: Prince Vladimir the Great
Description: Minor damage is noticeable on the right side.
Current Location Name: Church of the Holy Trinity in Gornji Adrovac

Name: Icon with St. Angelina of Serbia
Current Location Name: Church of the Holy Trinity in Gornji Adrovac

Name: Icon with the Virgin of the Three Hands
Description: The icon has a wide red frame on which are the signatures of the figures. In the inner field, on an ochre background, is the image of the Virgin Mary, holding the Christ Child in her right hand, who blesses and holds a scroll. A third hand of the Virgin is visible under his feet. The Virgin Mary has a black headdress and above it is the maphorion decorated with engraved ornaments.

Name: Icon with the Virgin "O All-Hymned Mother"
Description: The icon has a wide red frame. In the inner field, on an ochre background, there is the image of the Virgin Mary, facing right, holding with both hands the Child who is embracing her. The Mother of God has a red-orange maphorion decorated with engraved ornaments. The Christ Child is wrapped in an orange robe, leaving his shoulders and legs uncovered.

Name: Icon with Christ Pantokrator
Description: The icon has a wide red frame. In the inner field is  Christ the All-Keeper represented to the belt, holding an open gospel. He is dressed in a plaid chiton and ornamented with engraved ornaments himation. The icon is additionally placed in a profiled wooden frame.

Name: Icon with Saint Spyridon
Description: This icon depicts St. Spyridon the Bishop of Tremithus blessing and holding a Gospel book.

Name: Icon with the Virgin of the Sign
Description: The icon has a wide frame. In the inner field is the Virgin Mary in the Oranta pose presented to the waist, with a round medallion in front of her chest with a bust of the Child. The maphorion of the Virgin is decorated with engraved ornaments. The original inscriptions are illegible.

Name: Icon with the Archangel Michael
Description: Icon with the Archangel Michael standing, holding a sword and a shield.
Current Location Name: Church of St. Paul of Philanthropic Brotherhood of Men of Thessaloniki

Name: Icon with Saint Paraskeva Pyatnitsa
Description: The icon has a wide red frame. In the inner field against an ochre background is representated St. Paraskeva to the waist holding a cross and an open scroll. She is dressed in royal robes, with a crown on her head. Her upper garment and nimbus are decorated with engraved ornaments. A miniature Mandylion of Christ is inscribed above the saint's right shoulder.

Name: Icon with St. Nicholas the Wonderworker
Description: The icon has a wide red frame. In the inner field on an ochre background is represented St. Nicholas of Myra, wearing liturgical vestments, blesses and holds an open Gospel. In the background to the sides of his shoulders are busts of Christ and the Virgin Mary in round medallions.

Name: Icon with the Mother of God Vlachernitissa
Description: This representation of the Virgin and Christ child follows the Russian iconographic type of the Virgin of the Sign (Znamenie).

Name: The Crucifixion of Christ
Description: Icon depicting the Crucifixion of Christ at Golgotha.

Name: Icon with St. Nicholas the Wonderworker
Description: The icon has a wide reddish brown frame. In the inner field on an ochre background is the half-figure of St. Nicholas of Myra, wearing liturgical vestments, blesses and holds an open Gospel. In the background to the sides of his shoulders are the busts of Christ and the Virgin Mary in round medallions.

Name: Icon with St. Nicholas the Wonderworker
Description: The icon has a convex red frame (coffin). The half-figure of St. St. Nicholas of Myra is represented in the middle of the icon, wearing liturgical vestments, blesses and holds a closed gospel. The back of a throne is visible behind him. In the background on either side of his head are busts of Christ and the Virgin Mary. Inscriptions are not visible.

Name: Icon with the Crucifixion of Christ with Christ Pantocrator, St. Nicholas, St. George and St. Demetrius
Description: The icon has a wide red frame. The field is divided into four by the Crucifixion cross. In the center on a wide cross-shaped red field is the Crucifixion of Christ, above it is the blessing God Sabaoth in a cloud, to the left and right are the busts of the Virgin Mary and St. John the Theologian. At the top left, Christ All-Powerful blesses and holds a closed gospel. On the right is St. Nicholas the Wonderworker, blesses and holds a closed gospel. In the lower half on the left is St. George on horseback with a spear in his hand. On the right is St. Demetrius on horseback with spear in hand.

Name: Icon with the Virgin with the Christ Child
Description: On a dark, almost black background is presented half figure of the Mother of God, who holds the Christ Child on her left hand and points to him with the other. Christ blesses. Inscriptions can't be differed.

Name: Icon with Saint Charalambos
Description: The icon is housed in a box whose front glass is missing. The background is covered with thin foil ornaments. St. Charalambos is presented as half-figure, blessing and holding a closed gospel. Only the painting of his face and palms is visible.

Name: Icon with the Virgin of the Three Hands
Description: The icon is chromolithography on a tinplate. The Mother of God holds in her right hand the Christ Child who blesses. Their halos and the icon's frame are ornamented with blue and red color.

Name: Icon with the Resurrection of Christ with Feasts
Description: In the central part, the Resurrection of Christ and the Descent into Hell are presented one below the other. Around them in rectangular boxes are separate scenes of the Great Feasts. At the top: the Nativity of the Virgin Mary, the Entrance of the Virgin into the Temple, the Annunciation, the Nativity(?). On the right from top to bottom: the Baptism of Christ and the Transfiguration. On the left from top to bottom: the Representation of Jesus in the Temple and the Entrance into Jerusalem. At the bottom: Old Testament Trinity and Dormition of the Virgin. The icon's frame is black. The identifying inscriptions of each scene are illegible.

Name: Icon with Christ Pantokrator
Description: Icon with the full-length figure of Christ Pantokrator, who is depicted standing and holding the sphere with the left hand while blessing with the right.
Current Location Name: Church of St. Paul of Philanthropic Brotherhood of Men of Thessaloniki

Name: Icon with Saint John the Baptist
Description: Icon with Saint John the Baptist holding the cross with the left hand and blessing with the right one.
Current Location Name: Church of St. Paul of Philanthropic Brotherhood of Men of Thessaloniki

Name: Icon with Saint George
Description: St. George rides a white horse piercing a dragon in the mouth with his spear. The dragon is shown under the horse. In the background to the right, the kneeling figure of a maiden wearing a crown is depicted. In the upper right corner is a miniature image of Mandylion. The frame is orange-red.
Current Location Name: Church of Saint George, the town of Belogradchik

Name: Icon with Saint John the Baptist
Description: St. John the Forerunner is presented half-figure, holding a scroll with text and a chalice with the naked figure of the Christ Child (Christ the Victim). The frame of the icon is orange-red.
Current Location Name: Church of Saint George, the town of Belogradchik

Name: Icon with the Crucifixion of Christ with Virgin Kazanskaya, St. Nicholas, Arch. Michael and St. George
Description: The icon has a wide orange-red frame. The field is divided into four by the Crucifixion cross. In the center on a wide cross-shaped red field is the Crucifixion of Christ, above it is God Sabaoth, to the left and right are the busts of the Virgin Mary and St. John the Theologian. Between the arms of the cross in square boxes are: above - Virgin of Kazan and St. Nicholas the Wonderworker; below Archangel Michael on horseback and St. George on horseback slaying a dragon.
Current Location Name: Church of Saint George, the town of Belogradchik

Name: Icon with the Archangel Gabriel
Description: Icon with the Archangel Gabriel holding a lily.
Current Location Name: Church of St. Paul of Philanthropic Brotherhood of Men of Thessaloniki

Name: Icon with the Presentation of the Virgin Mary
Description: Icon depicting the Presentation of the Virgin to the church.
Current Location Name: Church of St. Paul of Philanthropic Brotherhood of Men of Thessaloniki

Name: Icon with the Annunciation
Description: The Annunciation of the Virgin Mary is portrayed with the Angel on the left and the Virgin on the right. The Holy Spirit is rendered flying over a lectern covered by a white cloth which is set between the two protagonists.
Current Location Name: Church of St. Paul of Philanthropic Brotherhood of Men of Thessaloniki

Name: The Last Supper
Description: Icon painted on metal leaf depicting the Last Supper
Current Location Name: Church of St. Paul of Philanthropic Brotherhood of Men of Thessaloniki

Name: Birth of the Virgin
Description: Icon painted on metal leaf depicting the birth of the Virgin.
Current Location Name: Church of St. Paul of Philanthropic Brotherhood of Men of Thessaloniki

Name: Icon with the Transfiguration
Description: Icon with the Transfiguration of Christ. At Christ's feet, saints Peter, James and John are seen lying or sitting, whereas Elijah and Moses are depicted standing on the right and left side of Jesus respectively.
Current Location Name: Church of St. Paul of Philanthropic Brotherhood of Men of Thessaloniki

Description: Portrait of Peter I from the book "Βιογραφίαι των Μεγάλων Ανδρών της Ρωσσίας".

Name: Icon with Christ Pantocrator
Description: The icon represents Christ Pantocrator holding a Gospel book.

Name: Virgin Mary Enthroned with Infant Christ
Description: The icon depicts the Virgin Mary enthroned with the Infant Christ. Virgin Mary's vestment is adorned with stars.

Name: St. Demetrius
Description: Saint Demetrius with scenes of his life and other saints.

Name: Dormition of the Virgin
Description: The icon depicts the Dormition of the Virgin and other scenes and saints.

Name: Icon with Saint Nicholas and scenes from his life
Description: Icon depicting St. Nicholas in the centre, surrounded by scenes from his life.

Name: Icon with the Archangel Michael
Description: Archangel Michael is depicted defeating Satan

Name: Iconostasis of St. Paraskevi, Metsovo
Description: The ten icons of the lower zone of the iconostasis are Russian. They were probably made between 1820 and 1840. They were offered by rich people from Metsovo who had settled in Russia.
Current Location Name: Church of Saint Paraskevi, Metsovo, Epirus

Name: Virgin Glykophilousa
Description: The wood was destroyed by bugs. The coloring is tainted and at some parts of the icon completely damaged.

Name: Icon with Saint Paraskeva
Description: Icon depicting Saint Paraskeva of Iconium with her symbolic attributes.

Name: Icon with Christ Pantocrator, Virgin Vlachernitissa and Saints
Description: The icon is divided into four registers; the upper register depicting the Christ Pantocrator on the left and Virgin Vlachernitissa on the right and the lower register showing two scenes with various saints.

Name: Icon with the Three Hierarchs
Description: This icon represents the Three Hierarchs. Basil the Great, Gregory the Theologian and John Chrysostom, are depicted in a traditional manner, blessing and holding the Gospels.

Name: Icon with the Apostles Peter and Paul
Description: The icon depicts the holy apostles Peter and Paul with Christ in the sky blessing them.

Name: Icon with Saint Paraskevi
Description: St. Paraskevi is presented to the knees, holding with both hands an icon of Christ in the tomb. The background is gold, with engraved decoration of boxes in which are inscribed flowers. The outer  frame of the icon is black. The inscription with the name of the saint on the background is illegible.
Current Location Name: Church of St. Paraskevi in Vidin

Name: Crucifixion
Description: A crucifixion of Russian provenance. Some damages. In the center the Crucifix and above God the Father and on the two sides of him are Virgin in the type of Hodegetria and probably Saint Nicholas and below are horseback Saints Demetrios and George. Left and right of the horizontal keraia are the Mother of God and John the Baptist. Dated in 17th or 18th C.

Name: Icon with the Virgin "Surety of Sinners"
Description: The icon has a wide orange-red frame. The Mother of God, with a crown on her head and an ornamented maphorion, holds the Christ Child in her left arm. The Christ Child, in a yellow robe and a crown on his head, takes His mother's hand.

Name: Virgin Mary and the Child (Vrephokratousa)
Description: Virgin Mary with infant Christ. Russian icon with frame from the same wood.   Condition: very good. 16th – 17th C.

Name: Saint Nicholas
Description: Saint Nicholas. Russian icon with frame from the same wood. The Saint is depicted in a bust, blessing, while holding a book with his left hand. On columns right and left are depicted busts of Christ and Virgin Mary. 16th – 17th C. These two icon prove to be important evidence for the relations of this area and Russia in a rather early age.

Name: Christ Pantokrator
Description: Pantokrator. Russian Icon without frame. 17th-18th C.

Name: Cross
Description: Cross with wooden frame from the top of an altarpiece. Depiction of the Crucifix and the ends of the cross which take the shape of clover are the symbols of the Evangelists. 18th -19th C.

Name: Resurrection
Description: Resurrection from Dodekaorton of an altarpiece. Folk icon of the 19th C.

Name: Annunciation
Description: Annunciation from Dodekaorton of an altarpiece. Folk icon of the 19th C.

Name: Icon with the Virgin of Smolensk
Description: The icon has a wide orange-red frame. The Mother of God is depicted half-figure, holding the Christ Child in her left arm and pointing at him. Her maphorion is decorated with floral ornaments. The Christ Child who is dressed in a black chiton and yellow himation blesses.

Name: Icon with the Resurrection of Christ with Feasts
Description: In the center of the icon is presented the Resurrection of Christ in two versions: at the top of the field is the resurrected Christ from the tomb, below is the Descent into Hell. Around the central field in 12 rectangular frames are presented scenes. Chronologically, starting from the top left, these are the Old Testament St. Trinity, Birth of the Virgin, Presentation of the Blessed Virgin Mary, Annunciation to Virgin Mary, Nativity of Christ, Presentation of Christ in the Temple, Baptism of Christ, Transfiguration of Christ, Entry into Jerusalem, Ascension of Christ, Dormition of the Virgin, Exaltation of the Holy Cross.

Name: Icon with St. Charalambos and scenes from his life
Description: In the center of the icon is the full-length St. Charalambos, who blesses and holds a closed gospel. In the background around the figure are presented four scenes from the life of the saint: on top left Crucifixion, on the right - Torture with fire. On the bottom left and right sides are scenes with the saint's trial. On the top left corner is an image of the Mandylion.

Name: Icon with the Virgin of Smolensk
Description: The icon is placed in a wooden box, the lid of which is missing. The icon has a wide orange-red frame. The Mother of God is depicted as half-figure, holding the Christ Child in her left arm and pointing at him. Her maphorion is decorated with floral ornaments. The young Christ, in a black chiton and yellow himation, blesses.

Name: Chalice set gifted by Rizares Brothers
Description:
Chalice, dimensions 0,46 x 0,17 m. It has a relief floral decoration. At the base of the brim there is the inscription:  ΑΦΡΜ (αφιέρωμα) των αδελφ(ών) Μάνθου και Γεωργίου Ριζάριδων εις Μνήμ(η) αυτών και των Γονέων αυτών [Dedicated by Rizari Brothers, Manthos and Georgios, in memory of them and their Parents].
Rizari brothers are the famous benefactors from Monodendri of Ioannina. In the main section of the chalice are medals made of enamel depicting Christ, Virgin Mary etc. At the base of the brim there is also a Russian inscription in capital letters. The chalice has a round cover which is adorned with relief decorations and small square enamel icons. It bears a workshop seal : Φ.Β. 1832.

Name: Chalice
Description: Silver chalice set donated by Ioannes Bitsinos in memory of him and his parents. Moscow 1933. Made in a Russian workshop.

Name: Icon with the Last Judgment
Description: This icon depicts various scenes of the aftermath of the second coming of Christ.

Name: Icon with the Presentation of the Virgin Mary
Description: Icon depicting the Presentation of the Blessed Virgin Mary into the Temple.

Name: Deesis, Annunciation, Saints
Description: Three different scenes are represented in two registers. In the upper part, is depicted the Deesis and in the lower part are represented the Annunciation of Virgin and a scene with Saints.

Name: Icon with the Resurrection of Christ with Feasts and scenes
Description: In the center of the icon is presented the Resurrection of Christ in two versions: at the top of the field is the resurrected Christ from the tomb with the prudent robber, below is the Descent into Hell. Around the central field in 12 rectangular frames are presented scenes. Chronologically, starting from the top left, these are the Old Testament St. Trinity, Birth of the Virgin, Presentation of the Blessed Virgin Mary, Annunciation to Virgin Mary (on top), Nativity of Christ, Presentation of Christ in the Temple, Baptism of Christ, Transfiguration of Christ, Entry into Jerusalem, Ascension of Christ, Dormition of the Virgin, Exaltation of the Holy Cross (on bottom). The icon has a narrow red frame.

Name: Icon with the Resurrection of Christ with scenes
Description: In the center of the icon is presented the Resurrection of Christ in two versions: at the top of the field is the resurrected Christ from the tomb with the prudent robber, below is the Descent into Hell. Around the central field in 12 rectangular frames are presented scenes. Chronologically, starting from the top left, these are the Old Testament St. Trinity, Birth of the Virgin, Presentation of the Blessed Virgin Mary, Annunciation to Virgin Mary (on top), Nativity of Christ, Presentation of Christ in the Temple, Baptism of Christ, Transfiguration of Christ, Entry into Jerusalem, Ascension of Christ, Dormition of the Virgin, Exaltation of the Holy Cross (on bottom). The icon has a narrow red frame and a wider gold interior one, with an engraved diamond-shaped ornament.

Name: Icon with the Crucifixion of Christ with Virgin Kazanskaya, St. Nicholas, Arch. Michael and St. George
Description: In the central cruciform field of the icon is the Crucifixion of Christ, above which is the God of Sabaoth. On the left there is a bust of the Virgin, on the right - of St. John the Theologian. In the upper left field is the Mother of God of Kazan, in the right - St. Nicholas the Wonderworker. In the lower left field is Arch. Michael on horseback, next to him - St. George on horseback. The frame of the icon is ochre.

Name: Icon with the Crucifixion of Christ with the Virgin of Kazan, St. Nicholas, Arch. Michael and St. George
Description: In the central cruciform field of the icon is the Crucifixion of Christ, above which is the God of Sabaoth. On the left there is a bust of the Virgin Mary, on the right - of St. John the Theologian. In the upper left field is the Mother of God of Kazan, in the right - St. Nicholas the Wonderworker. In the lower left field is Arch. Michael on horseback, on the right - St. George on horseback. The frame of the icon is ochre.

Name: Icon with Saint Nicholas
Description: The icon is pasted on an analogion and has an additional woodcarving frame, made in the first half of 20th century. St. Nicholas is presented half-figure, blesses and holds an open gospel. His vestments are ornamented with engraved floral ornaments. The frame of the icon is wide, ocher- yellow. The background is silver, on both sides of St. Nicholas in round medallions are the busts of Christ and the Virgin.
Current Location Name: Church of Saint Nicholas in Vidin

Name: Gold embroidered epitrachelion with dedicatory and liturgical inscriptions donated to Vatopedi monastery by the tsar of Russia Fiodor Ivanovitch
Icon with the Virgin of Vladimir
Description: The icon is a replica of the miraculous icon of the Mother of God of Vladimir. The garments of the Mother of God and the Christ Child are ornamented with silver motifs. The icon has a wide orange-red frame.
Current Location Name: Church of Saint Nicholas in Vidin

Name: Icon with St. Paraskeva
Description: Saint Paraskeva is represented to the knees, holding a cross and an open scroll with text. Two angels place a crown on her head. On both palms of the saint are placed metal plates, as well as on the nimbi of the angels and the saint. A miter-like crown with the image of the Christ Child in a bust is modeled on the plate of her nimbus. The background is decorated with incised circles. The icon is pasted in a profiled wooden frame dating from the twentieth century.
Current Location Name: Church of Saint Nicholas in Vidin

Name: Abraham's Hospitality
Description: Abraham’s Hospitality, dimensions 0,33 x 0,39 m., of Russian manner with wide painted frame.

Name: Icon with the Transfiguration of Jesus
Description: The icon has a double profiled frame (coffin), colored in dark blue and red. In the top half, Christ in white robes is in a round light, blessing and holding a scroll. On either side of him, facing him, are the prophet Elijah and the prophet Moses, who holds the tablet with the commandments. In the bottom part, apostles Peter and James have knelt, and ap. John has fell in the middle.
Current Location Name: Church of Saint Nicholas in Vidin

Name: Icon with Christ Pantocrator
Description: Jesus Christ is presented half-figure, blesses and holds an open gospel. His himation is ornamented with floral motifs. The icon has a wide orange-red frame.

Name: Icon with the Dormition of the Virgin
Description: Around the bed with the dead Mother of God are 11 apostles, two bishops and Christ with the soul of the Virgin in his hands. The frame of the icon is orange-red.

Name: St. George
Description: St. George, dimensions 0,52 x 0,71 m., of Russian manner, with golden background with stamp decorations.

Name: Dionysius Areopagites
Current Location Name: Church of Agia Eirēnē, Athens, Greece

Name: St. Ierotheos
Description: 19th Century Russian icon with St. Ierotheos from the church of St. Eirene in Aiolou Str., Athens.

Name: Christ Enthroned
Description: The icon with the Enthroned Christ, which hangs on the south wall of the Cathedral of Athens, with the equally early chronology 1850, […] it is likely that its unknown iconographer is Russian.

Name: St. Alexandra
Description: Depiction of Saint Alexandra with rich royal clothes.

Name: Theotokos with a gospel in a bust
Description: Icon depicting the Virgin Mary praying and holding an inscribed scroll.

Name: Icon with the Virgin Mary with scenes from her life and Dodecaorton scenes
Description: Icon depicting scenes from the life of the Virgin Mary with representations from the cycle of the Twelve Great Feasts.

Name: Icon with the Virgin Vladimirskaya
Description: The icon is a replica of the miraculous icon of the Mother of God of Vladimir. The frame of the icon is ornamented. Τhe color is monochrome, sustained in brown.

Name: Icon of the Holy Mandylion and Saints
Description: Icon depicting the Miracle of Saint Michael the Archangel and saints.

Name: Icon with the Virgin Kazanskaya, St. Nicholas, Arch. Michael and St. George
Description: The icon's field is divided into 4 fields. The Mother of God of Kazan and St. Nicholas, who are presented half figures, are above, below them are St. George on horseback and Arch. Michael on horseback. The frame is ornamented.

Name: Icon with the Three-handed Virgin
Description: The Mother of God is represented half figure, holding in her right hand the infant Christ, who blesses. Under the figure of Christ is seen the third hand of the Virgin. Their garments are decorated with engraved floral ornaments. The background is white. The icon has a wide orange frame.
Current Location Name: Church of the Nativity of the Blessed Virgin Mary, the town of Berkovitsa

Name: Icon with the Three-handed Virgin
Description: The object was probably first a home icon, later donated to the church. The Virgin Mary is presented half figure, holding in her right hand the infant Christ, who blesses. Under the figure of Christ is seen the third hand of the Virgin. Their garments are decorated with engraved floral ornaments. The icon has a wide orange frame. It is placed in a wooden profiled frame with glass.
Current Location Name: Church of the Nativity of the Blessed Virgin Mary, the town of Berkovitsa

Name: Icon with Mary Magdalene
Description: Saint Mary Magdalene is presented as half Figure with her head uncovered, wearing an ornamented garment, facing the image of the Crucifixion of Christ and wiping her tears with a cloth. The Crucifix of Jesus Christ is ​​presented on a hill. The icon has a wide orange frame.
Current Location Name: Church of the Nativity of the Blessed Virgin Mary, the town of Berkovitsa

Name: Icon with the Ascension of Jesus
Description: Oval-shaped icon depicting the Ascension of Jesus in the presence of his apostles.

Name: The Hospitality of Abraham
Description: This icon depicts the Old Testament Trinity, also known as "The Hospitality of Abraham" with the three angels who visited Abraham at the Oak of Mamre.

Name: Descent into the Hell, iconographical types of Theotokos and groups of Saints
Description: Icon depicting the descent of Christ into Hell with miniature scenes of various Saints.

Name: Icon with the Crucifixion of Christ and the Virgin Kazanskaya, St. Nicholas, Arch. Michael and St. Demetrius
Description: The icon is divided into four parts by the crucifix of the Crucifixion of Christ that is placed in the center of the composition. The busts of God Sabaoth, the Mother of God and St. John the Theologian are painted at the edges of the arms of the Cross. In the top two parts are presented a replica of the miraculous icon of the Virgin of Kazan (left) and an image of St. Nicholas the Wonderworker (right) depicted half figure. In the lower two parts,  Archangel Michael and St. Demetrius are both depicted on horseback. The icon has a wide orange-red frame.
Current Location Name: Church of the Nativity of the Blessed Virgin Mary, the town of Berkovitsa

Name: St. Paraskeue
Description: Icon of St. Paraskeue, probably by the hand of a Russian iconographer.

Name: Virgin Mary Glykophilousa
Description: The icon with the Virgin Mary (Glykophilousa) has a golden oklad and it is adorned with a diamond crown and other precious stones; it is a product of Russian workmanship, gifted by Ioannes Kapodistrias.
Current Location Name: Holy Monastery of Virgin Mary Platytera, Corfu

Name: Icon with the Crucifixion of Christ and the Virgin Kazanskaya, St. Nicholas, Arch. Michael and St. George
Description: The icon's field is divided into four by a crucifix form with an image of the Crucifixion of Christ with busts of the Mother of God, God Sabaoth and St. John the Theologian. In the top two fields are presented a replica of the miraculous icon of the Virgin Mary of Kazan, an image of St. Nicholas the Wonderworker, depicted half figure. In the bottom two fields are Arch. Michael on horseback and St. George on horseback. The icon has a wide orange-red frame.
Current Location Name: Church of the Nativity of the Blessed Virgin Mary, the town of Berkovitsa

Name: Icon with the Virgin Theodorovskaya
Description: The icon is a replica of the miraculous icon of the Mother of God Theodorovskaya. The garments of Virgin Mary and the child Christ have engraved siver ornaments. The icon's background is silver, with engraved rays that pass through the nimbus of the Virgin, the frame is wide and orange.

Name: Icon of Christ
Description: Despotic icon of Christ painted by a Russian painter whose name is not known. It was donated in 1867 by the Russian consul Georgios Duvnitzsky to the Church of St. Nicholas in Ermoupoli along with a despotic icon of the Mother of God. Both icons were transferred to the Church of the Resurrection of Christ in 1908.
Current Location Name: Church of the Resurrection of Christ, Ermoupoli, Syros

Name: Mother of God (Theotokos)
Description: Despotic icon with the Virgin painted by a Russian painter whose name is unknown. It was donated in 1867 by the Russian consul Georgios Duvnitzsky to the Church of St. Nicholas in Ermoupoli along with a despotic icon of Christ. Both icons were transferred to the Church of the Resurrection of Christ in 1908.
Current Location Name: Church of the Resurrection of Christ, Ermoupoli, Syros

Name: Virgin Mary Gorgoepeikoos
Description: Russian Bishop Uspensky found in the year 1855, in Misra (Old Cairo) Masr [as it is called today], an ancient icon of Virgin Mary which had the inscription “ΜΡ ΘΟΥ Η ΑΘΗΝΑΙΑ ΓΟΡΓΟΕΠΕΙΚΟΟΣ”. This icon was then forgotten [and] found [again] in the chapel of Forty Saints, the one beside the patriarchal church of St. George.

Name: Virgin Mary
Description: Icon of Virgin Mary made according to the Russian manner. It was gifted by Ioannes Lampros to the Christian Museum of Athens.

Name: Great Martyr Georgios
Description: Small Russian icon with the Great Martyr Georgios donated by P.Chatzopoulos to the Christian Museum, Athens
Brass icon of Russian artistry and on the brass printed icon of saints of Russian art. Gifted to the Christian Museum by Al. Xakoustes.

Name: Icon with the Virgin Tikhvinskaya
Description: The Mother of God is presented half figure on a gold background, holding the Christ Child in her left arm. The Infant, in an orange-gold robe, blesses and keeps a closed scroll. There are a lot of engraved floral ornaments in the background.

Name: Icon with Christ Pantocrator
Description: Christ is presented on a golden background, blessing and holding an open gospel. He is wearing a red chiton and dark blue himation. The background is decorated with engraved floral ornaments.

Name: Icon with St. John the Forerunner
Description: St. John the Forerunner is depicted on a gold background, holding a chalice with the figure of Christ the Sacrifice as a naked Infant to whom he points. He also holds an open scroll in his left hand. He is dressed in brown hair shirt and green himation.

Name: Birth of Christ
Description: Icon depicting the birth of Christ, sent from Moscow to San Giorgio dei Greci, now lost. The icon was gifted by Arsenios, Archbishop of Elassona.

Name: Icon with the Virgin Feodorovskaya
Description: The icon is a replica of the miraculous icon of the Mother of God Feodorovskaya. The maphorion of the Mother of God has engraved silver-gilted like floral ornaments. The Christ shirt is black, his himation is orange. The icon has a wide orange-red frame.

Name: St. George killing the Dragon
Description: Icon depicting St. George slaying the dragon sent from Moscow to San Giorgio dei Greci, now lost. The icon was donated by Arsenios, Archbishop of Elassona.

Name: Icon with St. John the Forerunner
Description: St. John the Forerunner is depicted on a gold background, holding a chalice with the figure of Christ the Sacrifice as a naked Infant to whom he points. He also holds an open scroll in his left hand. He is dressed in black hair shirt and ornamented himation. The icon is additionally placed in a profiled wooden frame, colored red.

Name: Icon with the Crucifixion of Christ with the Virgin Kazanskaya, St. Nicholas, Arch. Michael and St. George
Description: The icon field is divided into four by a crucifix with an image of the Crucifixion of Christ with busts of the Virgin and St. John the Theologian on the left and right, and God Sabaoth above it. In the top two fields are presented: a replica of the miraculous icon of the Mother of God of Kazan, an icon of St. Nicholas the Wonderworker, who are depicted half figure. In the bottom two fields are Arch. Michael on horseback and St. George on horseback. The icon has a wide orange-red frame.

Name: Icon with the Resurrection of Christ with Feasts
Description: In the center of the icon is presented the Resurrection of Christ in two versions: at the top of the field is the resurrected Christ from the tomb, as below is the Descent into Hell. Around the central field in 12 rectangular frames are presented scenes. Chronologically, starting from the top left, these are Birth of the Virgin, Presentation of the Blessed Virgin Mary in the Temple, Annunciation to Virgin Mary , Nativity of Christ (top), Presentation of Christ in the Temple, Baptism of Christ, Entry into Jerusalem, Transfiguration of Christ (middle), Ascension of Christ, the Old Testament St. Trinity, Dormition of the Virgin, Exaltation of the Holy Cross (bottom). The icon has a double frame: inner golden engraved and orange-red.

Name: Russian christening
Current Location Name: Church of the Holy Trinity in Gornji Adrovac

Name: Coronation of Stephen the First-Crowned, the first Serbian king
Description: The Church of the Holy Trinity in Gornji Adrovac was erected as a memorial to the Russian Colonel Nikolai Rajevski who died as a volunteer in the Serbian-Turkish wars of 1876. The interior painting program of the temple was subordinated to the memorial function with a portrait of Nikolaj Rajevski, but also to the foundations of Russian and Serbian national ideology. Sketches for the frescoes in the temple were made by the Russian artist Viktor Mikhailovich Vasnetsov. The inscription in the dome of the temple unequivocally says that the painting was made according to his templates. The designs for the painting program in Gornji Adrovac were realized by Dušan Obrenović, a painter from Kragujevac. The lower zones of the church are divided into northern and southern sides according to their themes. The Russian national ideology is prominent on the north side, and the Serbian one on the south. The most important saints and key events in Russian and Serbian medieval history are presented.
Current Location Name: Church of the Holy Trinity in Gornji Adrovac

Name: Portrait of Nikolaj Rajevski

Name: Encolpion
Description: Silver gilt enkolpion (pectoral) of Russian provenance. On the front there is a band of enamel studded with precious stones which surrounds an engraved representation of the Deesis: to the familiar composition of the full-length figures of the Mother of God and John the Baptist praying on either side of Christ enthroned is added the kneeling figure of Arsenios, also praying. On the reverse, there is another engraving, this time of Saint George on horseback slaying the dragon, surrounded by suplicatory inscription which supplies the name of the donor and the date (7104=1595/6).
Current Location Name: Hellenic Institute of Byzantine and Post-Byzantine Studies in Venice

Name: Virgin Tichvin
Description: Icon with a depiction of the Virgin of Tichvin, a Russian version of the Byzantine iconographic type of the Virgin Hodegetria.
Current Location Name: Hellenic Institute of Byzantine and Post-Byzantine Studies in Venice

Name: Virgin of Vladimir
Description: The icon was donated to the church of St. George of the Greeks in Venice by a certain Konstantinos Palaiologos in the name of Maria, widow of Dimitrios Palaiologos. This icon depicts the iconographic type of the Virgin Glykophilousa (Virgin of Tenderness), the Virgin of Vladimir. The icon was probably painted in a Moscow workshop.

Name: Christ Pantokrator
Description: Icon, extensively damaged on the painted surface, which fist appears in the inventories right at the end of the century, in 1700, with a depiction of Christ the Pantocrator holding an open Gospel in his left hand and blessing with the right, the palm turned outwards. This type, with Christ holding an open book and blessing with the palm of His hand turned outwards, is less common that that with the Gospel closed. It is encountered in Byzantine art from as early as the 12th century and in the next began to spread to Russia. Our icon dates from the 17th century, probably towards the end, a dating which matches the rendition of the face of Christ with its warm, human expression and moist eyes, in the type established in the 17th century by Simon Ušakov, the chief artist of the Oružejnaja palata in the Kremlin, who altered the traditionally-accepted type of portraiture and made it more natural.
Current Location Name: Hellenic Institute of Byzantine and Post-Byzantine Studies in Venice

Name: Triptych
Description: Smaill triptych, dated to ca. 17th century. In the triptych the silver gilt investment covers the representations , apart from the faces and hands of the figures. On the central leaf, there is a depiction of the Virgin and Child, in the type of the Virgin of Kazan, to whom full- length figures of three male and two female saints are praying on the left and right leaves respectively. According to the inscriptions, these figures are to be identified with Saints Antypas, Varlaam and Sergius, and Saints Paraskevi and Barbara. […] Triptychs of this type were destined for personal use, as is clear from their small dimensions, and could be hung up or taken with the believer when he or she moved elsewhere.

Name: St. Nicholas
Description: [In 1783] the Greeks of Venice accorded a warm welcome in Saint George’s church to Russia’s ambassador to Venice, Count Symeon Romanovič Vorontsov and his wife, Katherine, to whom they presented an icon of Saint Nicholas and a silver hanging-lamp.

Name: Mother of God Kazanskaya
Description: Only the faces of the two figures are not covered, though they are badly damaged, especially that of the Mother of God.

Name: Saints Cosmas and Damian
Description: Icon of Saints Cosmas and Damian, dated to the end of the 18th century. Both figures are rendered with tiny differences, mostly to do with minor variations in the clothing and in the position of the right hand. They are walking on rather rough ground. With flowers, and are raising their heads towards Christ, Who is depicted a little higher, between them, bursting through clouds and blessing with both hands raised.

Name: Christ
Description: "In 1836, Maria Pelegrini, who maiden name was Katrarou, gave the Greek church in Venice a Russian icon of Christ the Saviour, in accordance with the wish of her daughter Elenu, who had died at the age of sixteen. The icon, which probably dates from the beginning of the 19th century, bears a representation of Christ Pantokrator, (Spas Vsederžitel’)", as is written in the inscription. The gilt oklad does not cover the face and hands of Christ, Who is depicted blessing with His right hand holding an open Gospel in His lest, quoting the text from Matthew (11, 28-29). The icon was hung above the archiepiscopal throne, where it was to be found a little later, when it was recorded in the inventory of the year 1847. It is our belief that this is the same icons that the priests of Saint George’s still place in the same position during services. "

Name: Saints Sergius  and Nikon
Description:
Icon depicting Saints Sergius of Radonez and Nikon. Behind the saints, the monastery of Agia Lavra of St. Trinity is depicted . On the upper two angels hold an icon of Abraham's Hospitality. 

The icon is painted according to the western manner and the artist that created it is unknown.

Name: Virgin of Suzdal
Description: Russian icon depicting the Virgin with Jesus Christ in the type of Suzdal. It is decorated with silver oklad. The icon was probably made in Saint Petersburg ca. 1843.

Name: Virgin and the Child (Vrephokratousa)
Description: Icon depicting Virgin and the Child in the type of Vrephokratousa, surrounded by saints. It was donated to the Church of San Giorgio dei Greci by Diamantina Theodosiou in 1843. The icon is now lost.

In 1863, Countess Daria Ficquelmont died in Saint Petersburg amd her siter, Countess Caterina di Tiesenhausen sent a silver gilt hanging-lamp to her niece, the daughter of the departed sister, Princess Clara Aldringen who was in Venice, as a donation to St. George’s in memory of her relative

Name: Saint Spyridon
Description: Icon with Saint Spyridon, the Bishop of Trimythous. The icon is set in a broad wooden frame, at the four corners of which there is relief plant decoration depicting flowers, leaves and fruit. The gold background of the icon features relief patterns, while round its perimeter it is decorated with colours which imitate enamel, known in Russia at the time as “alla maniera veneziana”.

Name: Icon with Christ Pantocrator
Description: Jesus Christ is presented half figure, blesses and holds an open gospel. He is wearing a blue chiton and a red ornamented himation. The background behind the figure is gold-yellow. The frame is wide and orange-red.
Current Location Name: Church of the Dormition of the Virgin, Yasen village, Vidin Province

Name: Saints Constantine and Helen
Description: Icon depicting Saints Constantine and Helen painted in 1894 in Moscow by Fedor Sokolov.

Name: Icon with St. Stylianos
Description: St. Stylianos is presented half figure, facing left, holding a swaddled infant. The garments of the saint are ornamented. He is presented on a gold (yellow) background with a miniature image of the Holy Ubrus. The icon has a wide orange-red frame.
Current Location Name: Church of St. Paraskevi, Medkovets village, Montana Province

Name: Icon with the Virgin Tikhvinskaya
Description: The icon is a replica of the miraculous icon of the Virgin Tikvinskaya. The Mother of God is presented half figure on gold background, holding the Christ Child in her left arm. Christ, in an yellow robe, blesses and keeps a closed scroll. The icon has a wide orange-red frame.
Current Location Name: Church of St. Paraskevi, Medkovets village, Montana Province

Name: Icon with scenes of the Virgin Mary and Dodecaorton scenes
Description: Icon depicting the Resurrection and Descent to the Hell with numerous Dodecaorton scenes.

Name: Icon with Deesis, Saints and Donors
Description: Deesis icon depicting the enthroned Christ flanked by several holy figures.

Name: Icon with the Dormition of the Virgin
Description: Icon depicting the Dormition of the Virgin.

Name: Icon with the Theotokos Vrephokratousa
Description: Icon depicting Virgin Mary holding the Christ Child in the type of Kazanskaya.

Name: Icon with the Virgin Mary in Prayer (Hagiosoritissa)
Description: The icon depicts the Virgin Mary praying and holding an inscribed scroll.

Name: Icon with Christ Pantokrator
Description: Icon with Christ Pantokrator and four Saints.

Name: Icon with Saint Nicholas
Description: Icon with Saint Nicholas holding a Gospel book.

Name: Icon with an unidentified Hierarch
Description: Icon depicting St. Anthony flanked by the Guardian Angel and St. Domna.

Name: Icon with the Triumph of Theotokos
Description: Icon depicting the iconographic type known in Russia as the "Mother of God, Joy to All Who Suffer".

Name: Icon with the Resurrection of Christ with scenes
Description: In the center of the icon are presented the Resurrection of Christ and below the Descent into Hell. Around the central field in 12 rectangular frames are presented scenes. Chronologically, starting from the top left, these are the Old Testament St. Trinity, Birth of the Virgin, Presentation of the Blessed Virgin Mary, Annunciation to Virgin Mary, Nativity of Christ, Presentation of Christ in the Temple, Baptism of Christ, Transfiguration of Christ, Entry into Jerusalem, Ascension of Christ, Dormition of the Virgin, Exaltation of the Holy Cross. The icon has a wide orange-red frame. Τhe original inscriptions were erased, the names of the scenes were later written in Bulgarian on the frame.
Current Location Name: Church of St. Paraskevi, Medkovets village, Montana Province

The icon has a wide orange-red frame. Most of the inscription have been deleted.

Name: Saint Sergius
Description: Icon depicting Saint Sergius. It has a broad, carved wooden frame, the figure of Saint Sergius, who is identified in the inscription, is projected onto a gold background which forms a relief pattern. The gaunt figure of the white haired monk is represented face on, down to the waist. He is blessing with his right hand raised in front of his chest and is holding a closed scroll in his left. This iconographical type of the saint was one of the most widespread, particularly in the 19th century and the figure is rendered in the naturalistic style current at that time.

Name: Icon with the Resurrection of Christ with scenes
Description: In the center of the icon are presented the Resurrection of Christ, the Descent into Hell and Christ calling Peter. Around the central field in 12 rectangular frames are presented scenes. Chronologically, starting from the top left, these are the Old Testament St. Trinity, Birth of the Virgin, Presentation of the Virgin Mary to the Temple, Annunciation to the Virgin Mary, Nativity of Christ, Presentation of Christ in the Temple, Baptism of Christ, Transfiguration of Christ, Entry into Jerusalem, Ascension of Christ, Dormition of the Virgin, Exaltation of the Holy Cross.

Name: Icon with Saint Nicholas the Wonderworker
Description: The saint is presented half figure. He blesses and holds an open gospel. In the background on both sides of his head in two round medallions are the busts of Christ and the Virgin. The background is silver. The icon has a wide orange-red frame.

Name: Icon with Saint Nicholas the Wonderworker
Description: St. Nicholas is presented as half figure, dressed in richly ornamented liturgical vestments and a miter, blessing and holding an open gospel. On both sides of his head in the background Christ holds a closed gospel and the Virgin holds an omophorion. They are both in mandorla, stepping on clouds. The background imitates gold (colored varnish is placed on a silver base), with engraved ornaments. The nimbus of St. Nicholas and the frame have multicolored ornaments. The most outer frame is orange-red.

Name: Icon with the Virgin of Tikhvin
Description: The icon is a replica of the miraculous icon of the Mother of God of Tikhvin. The garments of the Mother of God and the Christ Child, also the nimbi, the background and the frame are covered with engraved ornaments.

Name: Icon with Saint Nicholas the Wonderworker
Description: The saint is presented as half figure, blesses and holds an open gospel. In the background on both sides of his head in two round medallions are the busts of Christ holding a gospel and Virgin holding an omophorion. The black background is filled with gold ornaments. The vestments of St. Nicholas and his nimbus have engraved ornaments.

Name: Icon with Sts. Constantine and Helen
Description: St. King Constantine and St. Helena stand on either side of a high cross with eight ends, erected on a cave with the skull of Adam. Above the cross in the clouds Christ blesses. The frame is orange-red.

Name: Icon with the Resurrection of Christ with Feasts
Description: In the center of the icon are presented the Resurrection of Christ, the Descent into Hell and Christ calling Peter. Around the central field in 12 rectangular frames are presented scenes. Chronologically, starting from the top left, these are  Birth of the Virgin, Presentation of the Blessed Virgin Mary, Annunciation to the Virgin Mary, Nativity of Christ, Presentation of Christ in the Temple, Baptism of Christ, Transfiguration of Christ, Entry into Jerusalem, Ascension of Christ, the Old Testament St. Trinity, Dormition of the Virgin, Exaltation of the Holy Cross.

Name: Icon with Resurrection of Christ and Feasts
Description: In the center of the icon is presented the Resurrection of Christ in two versions: at the top of the field is the resurrected Christ from the tomb, below is the Descent into Hell. Around the central field in 12 rectangular frames are presented scenes. Chronologically, starting from the top left, these are the  Birth of the Virgin, Presentation of the Blessed Virgin Mary, Annunciation to Virgin Mary, Nativity of Christ, Presentation of Christ in the Temple, Baptism of Christ, Transfiguration of Christ, Entry into Jerusalem, Ascension of Christ, Old Testament St. Trinity, Dormition of the Virgin, Exaltation of the Holy Cross.

Name: Icon with the Virgin Vladimirskaya
Description: The icon is a replica of the miraculous icon of the Mother of God of Vladimir. The nimbi are not outlined, but are in the form of a glowing. The background is dark brown, almost black. The frame is narrow and reddish-brown.

Name: Icon with Christ Pantocrator
Description: Jesus Christ is presented as half figure, blesses and holds an open gospel. His himation is decorated with floral ornaments. The background is silver, as the frame of the icon is wide and orange-red.

Name: Icon with the Virgin Feodorovskaya
Description: The icon is a replica of the miraculous icon of the Mother of God Feodorovskaya. The background is silver, covered with colored varnish olifa, the frame is wide and orange-red.

Description: The icon originates from the 19th century and depicts Various saints.
