Name: Icon with the Virgin Smolenskaya
Description: The icon is a replica of the miraculous icon of the Mother of God of Smolensk. The background is silver, as the frame is wide and orange-red.

Name: Icon with Saint Mitrophan of Voronezh
Description: The saint is presented to his waist, in archibishob's vestments, blessing and holding an episcopal scepter. Next to his head  is a miniature image of the Holy Mandylion in the background. The background is silver, as the frame is wide and oche.

Name: Icon with Saint Nicholas the Wonderworker
Description: St. Nicholas is presented as half figure, blesses and holds an open gospel. On both sides of his head in the background  are Christq, who holds a closed gospel, and the Virgin holding an omophorion. They are both in round medallions. The background imitates gold - colored varnish (olifa) is applied on a silver base,  while the frame is orange-red.

Name: Icon with the Crucifixion of Christ with St. Sergius of Radonezh
Description:
In the center of the icon is carved a casket, where a metel cast cross is pasted. On both sides of the Crucifixion of Christ are depicted St. Sergius of Radonezh on the left and unknown saint monk on the right. Two six-winged seraphim fly over the cross. The background is two-toned: dark (below) and gold (ochre) above. The frame is dark brown, bordered by a green and red line.
The metal cross has white, light and dark blue enamels on his front side. On the upper shoulder is depicted the Holy Mandylion, below it two flying angels with covered hands. In the center is Christ crucified on an 8-pointed cross. Below the cross are the Mother of God and Martha on the left, while on the right are St. John the Theologian and Longinus. Behind the cross is the panorama of Jerusalem, below the cross is the skull of Adam. Plant ornaments are engraved on the back of the cross.

Name: Icon with the Virgin Kazanskaya
Description: The icon is a eeplica of the miraculous icon of the Virgin of Kazan. Engraved decorations on nimbus, crown, maphoria and inner frame. The icon is placed in a gilded frame with carved ornaments that are missing today. There are two wax stamps on the back.

Name: Icon with New Testament Trinity and Coronation of the Virgin
Description: Christ, who is clothed in purple, is holding a large cross, and the God Sabaoth seats on clouds. Both of them place a crown on the head of the Mother of God, kneeling with folded arms before them. The crescent moon is depicted under the Mother of God. There is a dark blue circle under the feet of the Sabaoth. Above the heads of Christ and God is the Holy Spirit. There are cherubim around the clouds.

Name: Icon with the Virgin "Vzyskanie pogibshih"
Description: The icon is from a home iconostasis. The Mother of God is represented to the knee, sitting and holding the christ Child on her right side. She is hugging him with two clasped hands. Christ embracing his mother's neck, touching his cheek to her face. The epithet is illegible, but the iconography is close to the miraculous icon of the Virgin "Vzyskanie pogibshih" (Recovery of the Dead).

Name: Icon with the Virgin Feodorovskaya
Description: The icon is from a home icononstasis. It is a replica of the miraculous icon of the Mother of God Feodorovska. The icon has a frame with engraved geometric ornaments, while the background is silver. The inscriptions are illegible. There are illegible inscriptions in pencil on icon's back too.

Name: Icon with the Virgin Tikhvinskaya
Description: The icon is a replica of the miraculous icon of the Virgin of Tikhvin. The background is green, the nimbi of the Virgin and the Christ Child are red. The frame is brown, bordered by red and blue lines.

Name: Icon with the Great Holidays
Description: The icon comes from the 19th century and depicts the Resurrection of Christ with Great Feasts.
Current Location Name: Church of St. Nicholas Kumanovo, North Macedonia

Name: Icon with the Crucifixion of Christ, Virgin Icons and Saints
Description: The icon field is divided into four by the Crucifixion of Christ, which is depicted in the middle. Above Christ are the God Sabaoth and Holy Spirit, to the left and right are the sun and the moon, and below the cross is the skull of Adam. In the upper left field is represented the Virgin Mary "Joy to all who Grieve" (the Virgin as Queen with in full-length the Christ child in her arms, surrounded by various saints), on the right is the Virgin Feodorovskaya. In the lower left field is St. Nicholas the Wonderworker to the waist, to the right is St. Charalampius to the waist. The frames are quite wide and golden. St. Eudokia and St. Irene are represented in full length on the left frame, on the right frame is St. Anna.

Name: Icon with St. Nicholas the Wonderworker
Description: Saint Nicholas is represented half figure, blessing and holding a closed gospel. In the background on either side of his head in circular medallions are Christ, who holds a gospel, and the Virgin with an omophorion in her hands. The icon is covered with brass ornamented revetment with traces of gilding. The inscriptions are illegible.

Name: Icon with Saint Nicholas the Wonderworker
Description: The saint is represented half figure, blessing and holding an open gospel. In the background on either side of his head are Christ, who holds a gospel, and the Virgin with an omophorion in her hands. The background and frame are oche.

Name: Icon with Christ Pantocrator
Description: Jesus Christ is represented waist-high on a silver background, blessing and holding an open gospel. His chymation is richly ornamented. The icon has a wide orange-red frame.

Name: Icon with Virgin Kazanskaya
Description: The icon is a eeplica of the miraculous icon of the Virgin of Kazan. The frames, background and nimbi have engraved ornaments.

Name: Icon "The Virgin Apperiang to St. Sergius of Radonezh"
Description: The Virgin Mary in the center of the icon hands the abbot's staff to St. Sergius of Radonezh, who is kneeling before her. Behind the Virgin stand the apostles St. Apostle and St. John the Theologian and behind St. Sergius kneels his disciple Mihai. In the upper part, the New Testament Trinity is represented. The frame has multicolored floral ornaments.

Name: Icon with the Virgin of Kazan and scenes with miracles of the Icon
Description: In the center is the image of the miraculous icon of the Virgin of Kazan, around which there are 12 scenes with the story of finding the icon and the miracles it performed: The icon appears to the daughter of a warrior named Matrona; Matrona tells her mother about her vision; The Virgin appears to the maiden in a dream; Matrona and her mother tell  the archbishop about her vision; The mother digs but does not find the icon; Matrona finds the icon; The Archbishop ordered the icon to be taken to the church of St. Nicholas; The Archbishop and governors pray to the miraculous icon; They take the icon to the cathedral church; The king ordered to build a church for the icon and a nun monastery; The Virgin healed a man named Nikita who had an eye disease; The Mother of God miraculously restores the sight to blind Joseph.The icon have had a metal revetment, from which holes from the fastening are remained.

Name: Icon with Crucifixon of Christ with saints
Description: The Crucifixion of Christ divides the icon into four fields. In the above two are prophet Elijah  and a replica of the miraculous icon of the Three-handed Mother of God. In the lower two are St. George and St. Seraphim of Sarov. The frame has engraved geometric ornaments. The background is silver, covered with colored varnish, so it looks golden.

Name: Icon with St. Nicholas
Description: Saint Nicholas is represented  to his waist, blessing and holding an open gospel. The icon has a shallow cascket. The frame is wide and light brown.

Name: Icon with Archangel Michael and Sts. Florus, Laurus, Modestus and Blaise
Description: In the center of the icon arch. Michael holds the Holy Mandilyon. On either side of him are St. Florus and St. Laurus in the background, in front of them are St. Modestus and St. Blaise. The background in the upper part is golden, but in the lower part – like terrain is depicted.

Name: Icon with St. Nicholas the Wonderworker
Description: Saint Nicholas is depicted to his waist, blessing and holding an open gospel. In the background on both sides in round medallions are the busts of Christ with a gospel and the Virgin Mary with an omophorion. The icon has a wide orange-red frame. The background is silver. A metal cross gor wearing on the chest has been fixed to one side of the omophorus, which is kept separately. There are also traces of other votive revetments.

Name: Icon in three registers
Description: The icon is divided into three registers. In the first are The Virgin of Kazan, Descent into Hell and a bust image of St. Nicholas the Wonderworker. Second register consists 9 saints with illegible identifying inscriptions, one of them  is St. Zosima. In the third row in separate fields are: an unknown young saint or female saint, three unknown saints in joint composition and unknown saint.

Name: Icon with the Virgin Besednaya (The Appearing of the Virgin and St. Nicholas to the sexton Jurish)
Description: In the left part of the icon is St. Nicholas the Wonderworker in full length, against the background of a church building. In the right part, the Virgin Mary is seated under a tree. Between them is the small figure of a man facing the Virgin, above which is written his name - George. In the upper part was represented the figure of Christ All-Powerfull in clouds. The icon depicts the Apparition of the Virgin and St. Nicholas to the sexton George (Jurish).

Name: Icon with the Virgin "Vzyskanie pogubshih"
Description: The icon is a replica of the miracle-working icon of the Mother of God "Vzyskanie pogubshih" (Recovery of the Dead). The icon has a wide orange-red frame and a hanging loop.

Name: Icon in three registers
Description: The icon is divided into three registers. In the top right the Virgin of Kazan is represented and in the top left St. Nicholas the Wonderworker. In the bottom register St. Florus, St. Nicholas, Arch. Michael holding the Holy Mandylion, an unknown saint archbishop and St. Laurus are depicted.

Name: Icon with St. John the Baptist and life scenes
Description: St. John the Forerunneris depicted full length, holding a dish with Christ the Sacrifice and an open scroll. On the left is the scene of his Nativity, on the right is the Beheading of St. John the Baptist. In the upper left part in a circular medallion is the bust of God Sabaoth. The frame of the icon is wide and orange-red.

Name: Icon "Don't cry on Me Mother"
Description: In the foreground, the dead Jesus Christ is laid on a bier. Behind him is the Virgin Mary with her hands folded in front of her chest. The frame of the icon is wide and orange-red.

Name: Icon with Crist Pantocrator
Description: Jesus Christ is represented waist-high, blessing and holding an open gospel. The frame of the icon is wide and orange-red.

Name: Icon with St. Gerasimus of the Jordan
Description: St. Gerasimus is full-length, holding an open scroll. A lion stands before him. The background is a landscape with a river (the Jordan) and a large church. In the upper right corner, Jesus Christ blesses from clouds. The icon has a wide orange-red border.

Name: Icon with rhe Virgin Kazanskaya
Description: The icon is a replica of the miraculous icon of the Virgin of Kazan. The background is decorated with floral ornaments. The icon has a shallow double casket, the frame is brown-red.

Name: Icon with Virgin of the Sign
Description: The icon is a replica of the miraculous icon of the Virgin of the Sign. The frame is wide and orange-red.

Name: Icon with St. Nicholas the Wonderworker
Description: The saint is represented to the waist, blessing and holding an open gospel. In the background on both sides are the busts of Christ with a Gospel and the Virgin with an omophorus in hands. The icon has an inner gold and an outer orange-red frames. The background is silver. A metal cross for wearing on the chest was attached to one side of the saint's omophorus, which is stored separately now. There are also traces of other votive revetments.

Name: Icon with the Virgin Vladimirskaya
Description: The icon is a replica of the miraculous icon of the Virgin of Vladimir. The background is dark red, the frame is brown. The icon has a hanging loop.

Name: Icon with the Virgin of the Sign
Description: The icon is a replica of the miraclous icon of the Virgin Mary of the Sign. It has a wide orange-red frame.

Name: Icon with Christ Pantocrator
Description: Jesus Christ is represented waist-high, blessing and holding an open gospel. The background and garments of Christ are silver in color and ornamented. The icon has a double frame, colored orange and brown.

Name: Icon with Saint Barbara
Description: Saint Barbara is represented in a half-length portrait, on a silver background. In the upper left corner of the icon, next to the Saint's head, a miniature Holy Mandylion is depicted. Saint Barbara turns her gaze towards Mandylion and at the same time she points to it with her raised right hand. The icon has a wide orange-red painted frame.

Name: Icon with the Head of St. John the Forerunner
Description: The severed head of St. John the Forerunner, with closed eyes, is shown on a plate, which is placed on a table (?) covered with a yellow tablecloth. The background of the upper half of the icon is silver and orange-red at the lower half. The icon has a wide orange-red frame.

Name: Icon with the Birth of the Virgin Mary
Description: In the central part of a building with three parts (wings) is the Birth of the Virgin, in the left wing is St. Joachim, in the right is the Conception of the Holy Virgin - the Meeting of St. Anna and St. Joachim. Above the side wings are the figures of the Virgin Mary's parents.

Name: Icon with Cyril and Methodius
Description: The holy brothers are  presented full-length, on a landscape background. St. Cyril holds a scroll with the Cyrillic alphabet, as St. Methodius holds a tall processional cross and a chalice. The icon has a wide ochre frame. The signature of the icon-painter is in the lower left corner. The icon is painted by Vasilii P. Guryanov, who worked in Moscow, in 1902.

Name: Icon with the Dormition of the Virgin Mary
Description: The standard iconography of the scene of Dormition of the Virgin Mary is presented, without the images of women and without the episode with the angel cutting off the hands of Jephonius too.

Name: Icon with the Holy Mandylion
Description: The white cloth with the image of the Mandylion is held by two full-length angels standing on clouds. The icon has a wide orange-red frame.

Name: Icon with St. Nicholas the Wonderworker
Description: Saint Nicholas is represented to the waist, blessing and holding a closed gospel. On either side of his head in clouds, Christ hands him a gospel, and the Virgin - an omophorus. The icon had a silver-plated copper revetment, which was removed (Inventory number ВИИ 516).

Name: Icon with Saint Pantaleon
Description: The saint is represented to his knees, holding a medicine box and a little spoon. The icon is framed and under glass.

Name: Icon with Christ Pantocrator
Description: Jesus Christ is represented to the waist, holding an open gospel. His garments are silver-ornamented. The icon has a wide orange-red frame, as the background is silver.

Name: Icon with the Virgin Vladimirskaya
Description: The icon is a replica of the miraculous icon of the Virgin of Vladimir. The icon has a wide orange-red frame, the background and figures' nimbi are silver, their garments also, but ornamented.

Name: Icon with Saint Nicholas
Description: The saint is represented to the waist, blessing and holding a closed gospel. Only the face and both hands are completed, the rest of the details are just outlined. The icon has had a icon revetment,  that covered the entire surface, except for the face and palms, but now it is missing. There are no inscriptions.

Name: Stole in Makrinitsa II
Description: Russian stole from woven gold (χρυσούφαντο) with floral decoration.

Name: Phelonion from Russia in Makrinitsa III
Description: Russian phelonion from woven gold with floral decoration

Name: Chalice in the Monastery of Timios Prodromos (Skete Veroias)
Description: Gilded silver Chalice. 1768. Gift of Catherine the Great. On its base, we find the names of Romanov family. 18 centimenters (height), 6,5 centimeters (height of the upper part [κούπα], 8 centimeters (diameter of κούπα), 12 centimeters diameter of the base.

Name: Serafeim Sarovsky
Description: The icon represents the Russian saint Serafeim of Sarov (Σεραφείμ Σαρόβσκυ) in the usual way; as an aged person, with a white scapular in a gold decoration, with a yellow halo. The field is dark (see SourcePassage/1062 for a more detailed description in Greek). There are Russian insciptions on the back side of the icon, which show that the icon was made in 1915. The stamp shows that the icon received the benediction of the abbess and the nuns of the female monastery having the saint's name. From the upper inscription, we learn that the icon belonged to the members of the Romanov family (one of the Key words gived here) and was gifted to Simonos Petra Monastery in 1987.

Name: St Mitrofan, bishop of Voronezh, the miracle-working
Description: Icon of St Mitrofan of Voronezh, the miracle-working. The saint ia represented to hold his episcopal crozier and to give his benediction (for a more detailed description in Greek, see SourcePassage/1051). Gold decoration. Icon that could be dated from 1825 to 1925, without inscription, in good state of conservation. The icon is in Simonos Petra Monastery.

Name: Osios Mitrofan bishop of Voronezh
Description: Icon of St Mitrofan of Voronezh. The bishop is represented to give his benediction with his right hand (for a more detailed description in Greek, see SourcePassage/1053). Icon made in 1840, with Russian inscription. It is in Karakalou Monastery.

Name: St Mitrofan of Voronezh
Description: Icon of St Mitrofan of Voronezh. The saint is represented as an old person, having black cloths and  a white scapular, with his episcopal crozier, giving his benediction with his right hand. The decoration is in gold. His halo is yellow and the field is dark. Icon dated from 1800 to 1900, with Russian inscription. It is in Pantokratoros Monastery.

Name: Icon with the Crucifixion of Christ, the Virgin of Kazan and Saints
Description: In the center of the icon the Crucifixion of Christ is depicted, above it - a bust of God Sabaoth, on the sides - busts of the Mother of God and St. John the Theologian. In the four parts around the Crucifixion there are: the Virgin of Kazan and a waist-length image of St. Nicholas of Myra on the top part and below – the figures of arch. Michael and St. George on horses. The icon has an orange-red frame.
Current Location Name: Museum of the Bulgarian Revival and Constituent Assembly

Name: All Saints (Αγιοι Πάντες)
Description: The icon is divided in two parts. In the inferior part, there are different saints, prophets and martyrs; in the middle, there is a table (covered by a green covering) with a big Holy Cross and small ustensils. In the upper part, there is a cloudy sky, with Virgin Mary (having a blue coat) and John the Forerunner (having a closed scroll in his left hand and giving his benediction with his right hand). John the Forerunner wears a green coat and inside, a cloth made by camel's hair, whose colour is olive brown. On the clouds, we see the Christ and Father God in their thrones. The Christ has in his left hand a closed Gospel and gives his benediction with his right hand. There are different beasts behind them (for a more detailed description in Greek, see SourcePassage/1021)

Name: St Sergius and St Germanos
Description:
There are two saints represented here, the founders of the Valaam Monastery, St Sergius and St Germanos, in their monastic vestments and with halos. On the left, St Sergius holds an open stroll (with Slavonic letters) in his right hand, whereas St Germanos holds another open stroll in his left hand and shows to the Monastery of Varlaam with his right hand. The Monastery is represented as usual. The inscription is not readable. There is a little scene in the middle of the sky showing probably the Transfiguration.
Icon made between 1900 and 1970.

Name: Panagia Hodegetria
Description: Icon close to the iconographic type of the Virgin of Vladimir. The colours are not in good condition. Icon made between 1700 and 1850. With inscription in Russian.

Name: Three Saints
Description: Three saints are represented here: on the left, an aged, sitted saint who writes on a scroll (probably John the Theologician); in the middle, there is a female figure, holding a child; and on the right, another female figure who is turned towards the central fugure. Russian icon made between 1800 and 1910, with no inscriptions. On its back side, it is written: "skete of Saint Andrew and a name".

Name: Panagia Hodegetria
Description: Virgin with child. The icon is covered by an embroidered and painted covering. On the left side, there is the inscription "Virgin Old-Russian"(«Θεοτόκος Παλαιορωσική»). Made probably between 1800 and 1910. Inscription in Russian.

Name: Funeral Lamenation
Description:
The Christ is represented recumbent under the Cross. Around him, there are different saints (their name is mentioned in their halo): on the left, Saint Joseph holds the Christ's head; and on the right, next to the Christ's feet is Saint Nicodemus. Next to Saint Joseph is one of the myrophore women, Saint John the Theologian is on his knees on the right side of the woman, and the Virgin Mary is next to him. Mary Magdalene is on the right side of the Virgin. In the background, there are two myrophore women and a sitted archangel. In the corners, there are the heads of the Evangelists and also symbols of the Crucifixion (like the column with a thorn crown [...] stairs, lance, lance with sponge, cock). In the upper part, the is the head of God surrounded by clouds, who is blessing with his two hands. In front of him there is a globe with a cross and below a dove representing the Holy Spirit. On his left, there is the Moon and on his right, the Sun.
In the lower part of the composition, there is a hand-made inscription with the name of the bishop, the location on Mount Athos and the year 1880. The engraving on the cloth was made in Constantinople, as it is specified on the margin.

Name: Burial of Christ
Description:
The Christ is represented recumbent under the Cross. Around him, there are different saints (their name is mentioned in their halo): on the left, Saint Joseph holds the Christ's head; and on the right, next to the Christ's feet is Saint Nicodemus. Next to Saint Joseph is one of the myrophore women, Saint John the Theologian is on his knees on the right side of the woman, and the Virgin Mary is next to him. Mary Magdalene is on the right side of the Virgin. In the background, there are two myrophore women and a sitted archangel. In the corners, there are the heads of the Evangelists and also symbols of the Crucifixion (like the column with a thorn crown [...] stairs, lance, lance with sponge, cock). In the upper part, the is the head of God surrounded by clouds, who is blessing with his two hands. In front of him there is a globe with a cross and below a dove representing the Holy Spirit. On his left, there is the Moon and on his right, the Sun.
In the lower part of the composition, there is a hand-made inscription with the name of the bishop, the location on Mount Athos and the year 1903. The engraving on the cloth was made in Constantinople, as it is specified on the margin. Inscription in Russian.

Name: Saint Nikita the Martyr and Saint Eirini (Μάρτυρας Νικήτας και Αγία Ειρήνη η Μεγαλομάρτυς)
Description: Saint Nikita with military cloths and a purple coat is on the left side, in military vestments; and Saint Eirini with a yellow dress and a purple coat on the right side. Both of them have in their right hand a palm and in their left hand a cross. The ground is dark green. On a cloud, there is Christ giving his benediction to the saints. The Russian insciptions give the names of the saints. Icon made between 1750 and 1910.

Name: Resurrection of Christ (Ανάσταση του Χριστού)
Description: The Christ is represented in a cloud, accompanied by two angels in the lower section. The icon is covered by a metallic revetment, which allows only some details to be seen. The added, nailed halos are also metallic. Probably made between 1800 and 1910. Inscriptions in Russian.

Name: Agioi (Saints)
Description:
Two-faced icon. The one side is divided in three parts (for a more detailed descrition, see SourcePassage/1018). The upper part shows the Virgin with child (on the left), the Christ in the middle and a saint (probably St Nicolas) on the right. The part in the middle shows different saints (some of them are bishops, according to their vestments). The icon is quite damaged, especially in the lower part, which has three openings (exactly as the upper one) but the scenes cannot be distinguished.
On the other side of the icon, there is Virgin Axion Esti, holding the hand of Christ with her right hand. The Christ has a stroll with a text in Old Slavonic.
Icon made between 1700-1910, with Russian inscription.

Name: Silver-gilt and niello icon of the Kazanskaya Mother of God
Description:
Description: the faces finely painted, the oklad repoussé decorated with floral motifs, the Virgin's halo centred with a crown of coloured pastes, St Tatiana standing full length on the right border, the text in niello below citing the Troparion for the feastday of the Kazanskaya Mother of God.



Inscription on the reverse reads:
 'This holy icon of the Holy Mother of Kazan was presented on 17th November 1891 in Tula, painted on a cypress board more than 100 years ago. The silver-gilt oklad was made in 1795 and its kiot made out of red wood with gilding, under glass. It was presented by the tradeswoman Elizabeth Yegorovna Sheldyaeva to the Monastery Rossikon on the Holy Mount Athos to the holy Great Martyr and Healer Panteleimon. The  icon was inherited as a blessing from her father Yegor Osipovich and her Mother Tatiana Mikhailovna Sushkin in honour of the blessed marriage with Ivan Ivanovich Sheldyaev in memory of the passing of George, John 2, Tatiana 2, Elizabeth 2, Paraskeva, baby Alexander and for the good health of Elizabeth, Merkul, Catherine, Mary, Alexandra and all her relatives.The grandaunt of Father Archimandrit Makarij Sushkin'.

Name: Panagia Glykophilousa
Description: The icon is close to the Russian type of the Virgin Kasperovskaya (for a more detailed description in Greek, see SourcePassage/1020). An insciption in Russian on the upper part informs us that this is the wonder-working icon of the Virgin Kasperovskaya. The nailed halos have been added separately (Πρόσθετα μεμονωμένα καρφωτά φωτοστέφανα). Icon made between 1800 and 1920.

Name: Icon with the Virgin with the Infant
Description: Icon wiith the Virgin of Smolensk. Virgin Mary is depicted from the waist up, holding Jesus Christ in her left hand. The Child, portraited in frontal pose is resting on his Mother's arm and at the same time he is blessing with his right hand. The heads of both figures are surrounded by a halo. In addition, the top of the Virgin's halo is decorated by a five-pointed crown. Only minor damages are detected on the painting surface.
Current Location Name: Korgialenio Historical and Folklore Museum of Argostoli

Name: Icon with the Crucifixion of Christ, the Virgin of Kazan and Saints
Description: In the center of the icon is the Crucifixion of Christ, above it a bust of God Sabaoth, on the sides - busts of the Mother of God and St. John the Theologian. In the four parts around the Crucifixion are: top - the Virgin of Kazan and a waist-length image of St. Nicholas of Myra; bottom are the figures of arch. Michael and St. George on horses. The icon has an orange-red border.
Current Location Name: Museum of the Bulgarian Revival and Constituent Assembly

Name: Icon with the Crucifixon of Christ, the Virgin of Kazan and Saints
Description: In the center of the icon is the Crucifixion of Christ. In the four parts around the Crucifixion are: top - the Virgin of Kazan and a waist-length image of St. Nicholas of Myra; on the bottom are the figures of arch. Michael and St. George on horses. The icon has an orange-red border.
Current Location Name: Museum of the Bulgarian Revival and Constituent Assembly

Name: Panagia of Kazan
Description: The Virgin Mary has big eyes; her hands are not visible. The child gives his benediction with his right hand. Mary hasa purple coat with stars, and the child a dark cloth and a purple coat. They have both halos. The fiels is of a light colour. The icon has an embroidered revetment. There is a sticker with the number 2475, in the lower part, on the left, on the back side. There is an inscription in Russian identifying the iconographic subject in the lower part, on the frame.

Name: Panagia Vrefokratousa
Description: The icon is covered by a metallic revetment and because of this, no details are visible. There is a saint with military vestments in the lower part. He is holding a banner and lies down. It seems like the saint does not belong to the icon: as if he was added because of an erroreous revetment.

Name: Panagia of Kazan
Description: The Virgin has a purple coat with gold details. The Christ also wears gold cloths. They both have halos. The field is of beige colour.

Name: Panagia Vrefokratousa
Description: The hands of the Virgin are not visble. She has a purple coat with gord details and the cloths of Christ are also gold. They both have halos and the field is of beige colour.

Name: Panagia Hodegetria
Description: The Virgin Mary wears a purple coat. The Christ gives his benediction with his right hand (for a more detailed descripton in Greek, see SourcePassage/1099). Details in gold. With metallic revetment.

Name: Panagia of Kazan
Description: The hands of the Virgin Mary are not visible. The Christ, wearing dark cloths and a purple coat,  gives his benediction with his right hand. Both have halos. The Virgin has a purple coat (μαφόριο) with stars (one on her shoulder and the other one on her front). The field is of alight colour.

Name: Panagia of Kazan
Description: The Virgin Mary wears a purple coat; her hands are not visible. The Christ gives his benediction with his right hand. Both wear halos. The field is of dark colour.

Name: Virgin Mary with the Child
Description: The composition centers around the Virgin dressed in a maphorion decorated with geometric motifs on the edges of the garment. She carries her Son who is depicted like a child. The heads of the characters touch each other and, to complete the gesture of maternal affection, the child’s arm embraces the mother’s neck. The Virgin’s left hand is bent over her chest, fingers outstretched, pointing to Jesus. Both characters have circular haloes. The composition is completed by the background loaded with vegetal motifs, and the edge is marked by a wide band with the motifs of the eight-cornered star and flowers.

Name: Όσιος Γερμανός Αρχιεπίσκοπος του Καζάν, Όσιος Γιούρι Αρχιεπίσκοπος του Καζάν και Όσιος Βαρσανούφιος επίσκοπος του Τβερ
Description: Three hierarchs: at the center, Osios Yuri, archbishop of Kazan, who gives his benediction with his right hand and has a banner on the other hand. On his left, Osios Germanos, archbishop of Kazan, who holds a closed Gospel. And on the right, Osios Barsanuphius, bishop of Iver, holding a cross with his right hand. The Virgin Mary of Kazan also appears on the upper level, in the middle, inside a cloud. The field is in gold.

Name: Panagia of Kazan
Description: The Christ wears a purple coat and gives his benediction with his right hand. The details are not visible because of the metallic revetment.

Name: Saint Nikita
Description: The saint is usually rendered with a whip in his hand while hitting a human-looking creature who embodies the demon who tried to tempt him. His image was a talisman against Devil’s cunning and a symbol of the active involvement of the fighting spirit, as a sacred extension of the struggle against those who wanted to change the old faith.

Name: Icon with the Resurrection of Christ/Descent into Hell and Twelve Secenes
Description: In the center of the icon are presented the Resurrection of Christ, the Descent into Hell and Christ called Peter. Around the central field in 12 rectangular frames are presented scenes. Chronologically, starting from the top left, these are the  Birth of the Virgin, Presentation of the Blessed Virgin Mary, Annunciation to Virgin Mary, Nativity of Christ, Presentation of Christ in the Temple, Baptism of Christ, Transfiguration of Christ, Entry into Jerusalem, Ascension of Christ, Old Testament St. Trinity, Dormition of the Virgin, Exaltation of the Holy Cross.
Current Location Name: Museum of the Bulgarian Revival and Constituent Assembly

Name: Panagia Hodegetria
Description: Panagia Hodegetria, at a heigh of 3/4, with imperial crown, holding with her left hand the Christ. The icon is covered by a rich, gold revetment with many details and rich colours in the halos. The icon was photographed without the revetment: the Virgin  wears a purple coat and the field is dark brown.

Name: Christ, Saint Sergius and Saint Barlaam of Khutyn
Description: The Christ is represented according to the iconographic type of the Saviour of Smolensk, in a standing position. On the lower part, there are two persons on their knees. On the left, there is saint Sergius and on the right, saint Barlaam of Khutyn. The icon is covered by a metallic revetment.

Name: Saint Nicholas and other saints
Description: There are six saints represented here. Above them, there is a cloud, with the Christ giving them his benediction. At the center of the composition is saint Nicholas. On his left, there are saint Antony, (most probably) saint Nikitas and another saint whose name is not easy to distinguish. On his right, there are saint Barlaam and another saint. The details are not visible because of the metallic revetment.

Name: Second Coming (Δευτέρα Παρουσία)
Description: The icon represents the Second Coming in an unusual way and has insciptions in Russian and in Georgian. It is a Georgian icon printed in 1895, after the approval of the Archibishopric of Moscow (for more iconographic details in Greek, see SourcePassage/1061).

Name: Saint Nicholas
Description: Six printed images representing Saint Nicholas, who is giving his benediction with his right hand. On the upper part, in the corners, there is the heads (προτομές) of the Christ on the left and of the Virgin on the right.

Name: Panagia of Pochayev
Description: The engraving represents the Virgin Mary having in her arms the Christ. Both of them wear imperial crowns. Perimetrically, there is a geometrical decoration. An inscription on the lower part informs us that this is the Virgin of Pochayev. On the lower part, there is also a shepherd on his knees with his flock of sheep.

Name: Panagia Galaktotrophousa
Description: The icon represents the Virgin Mary Galaktotrophousa with purple coat and an imperial crown that two angels (on their knees in a cloud) put on her head. She gives her breast to the Christ. Both of them have simple halos, defined by a red line. The Christ wears a light blue cloth and a gold coat. The field is yellow. On both sides, on the upper level, there are medals with saints (St Nicholas on the left and st John the Forerunner on the right, who holds a tray with his cut head). According to an inscription below, this is the copy of a wonder-miracle icon. Other inscriptions explain that the permission was given in Kiev in 1907. The Russian skete of Prophet Elijah is also mentioned.

Name: Panagia Eleousa and its miraculous appearance
Description: The icon is divided in two parts. The upper part, which is the bigger, shows Panagia Eleousa, wearing a purple coat, an imperial crown and holding the Christ. Where the two parts meet, an inscription mentions that this is the miraculous appearance of the Virgin of Pochayev. This is represented in the lower part: the Virgin is inside a big flame, having a blue cloth and a purple coat and holding a cross with her right hand. She looks at a kneeled priest on the left, while on the right there is a shepherd with a flock of sheep.

Name: Panagia Vrefokratousa
Description: The Virgin Mary has a purple coat and an imperial crown. The Christ (that she holds in her arms) has also an imperial crown. He has a white cloth and a gold coat (Εικονίζεται η προτομή της Παναγίας Βρεφοκρατούσας. Η Παναγία στρέφεται προς τα αριστερά. Το θείο βρέφος ακουμπάει το πρόσωπο της Παναγίας). There is a symbol on the lower part (Στο κάτω τμήμα αποδίδεται κάποιο σύμβολο).

Name: The miraculous appearance of the Virgin of Pochayev
Description: The Virgin is in the middle of the scene, inside a big flame. She wears a purple cloth and a blue coat. She holds a scepter with her right hand. She looks at a kneeled priest on her left, while on the right there is a kneeled shepherd with a flock of sheep. There are trees around them.

Name: Panagia of Pochayev
Description: The icon represents the miraculous appearance of the Virgin of Pochayev. The Virgin is in the middle of the scene, inside a big flame. She wears a purple cloth and a blue coat. She holds a scepter with her right hand. She looks at a kneeled priest on her left, while on the right there is a kneeled shepherd with a flock of sheep. There are trees around them.

Name: Osios Job of Pochayev
Description: The icon represents St Job of Pochayev according to the traditional way. He is dressed as a monk, he gives his benediction with his right hand and has a stick in his left hand. He has a long white beard. The field is of green and brown colour.

Name: Joy to All Who Suffer (Χαρά πάντων των θλιβομένων)
Description: The Virgin Mary stands in the middle, wearing a white coat. On both sides, there are archangels and on the lower level, sick people suffering from different diseases. Above the head of the Virgin, there is a text. On the upper level, in the clouds, the Christ gives his benediction to the other figures below. Perimetrically, there is a geometrical decoration.

Name: Panagia Vrefokratousa with patients
Description: The Virgin Mary stands in the middle and holds the Christ with her left hand. Both of them wear imperial crowns and richly decorated halos. The Christ holds a globe with cross with his right hand. The Virgin wears a white cloth, which covers her head, a purple cloth and a blue dress with rich gold embroideries. The Christ wears a simple white cloth. There are two standing angels, on the left and the on the right. Below, there three people (two on the left and one on the right) suffering from different diseases (blind, disabled etc.). Perimetrically, the frame has a geometrical decoration (Περιμετρικά η κορνίζα φέρει γλυπτό-χαρακτό γεωμετρικό διάκοσμο).

Name: Theotokos and patients
Description: The Virgin Mary stands in the middle, dressed in dark colours and has in her hands a purple piece of cloth. Perimetrically, there are smaller figures of saints and of patients; above them archangels are standing. The Virgin Mary gives her blessing to them. The icon is damaged, but most probably it is the Virgin "Joy to All Who Suffer" (Η εικόνα είναι εν μέρει φθαρμένη, άλλα πιθανότατα πρόκειται για την σκηνή ВСЕХ СКОРБЯЩИХ РАДОСТЬ; μτφ. «Χαρά όλων των θλιμμένων»). Above, the Virgin's head, there is the head of the Chist (represented as a young man), who gives his benediction with his right hand; he wears a blue cloth and a purple coat. The field is of dark colour.

Name: Theotokos and patients
Description: The Virgin Mary stands in the middle, holding the Christ with her left hand. Both of them have halos with imperial crowns. The Virgin wears a purple coat and the Christ a green cloth with a gold coat. He holds with his left hand a globe and with the right hand he gives his benediction. The Virgin holds with her right hand an open scroll. On the right and left, there are archangels and below them, patients suffering from differnet diseases. There is a scroll with a text above the head of the Virgin. In ths clouds, on the upper part, there is God the father who gives his benediction to the figures below. In the corners, on the left and right, there is the sun and the moon.

Name: Theotokos and patients
Description: The Virgin Mary stands in the middle, holding the Christ who gives his benediction with his right hand. On the left and right, perimetrically, there are smaller figures of saints and sick people. Above them, there are archangels. On the upper level, there are two saints on each side. The icon is damaged (Η εικόνα είναι εν μέρει φθαρμένη. Πρόκειται για την σκηνή ВСЕХ СКОРБЯЩИХ РАДОСТЬ; μτφ. «Χαρά όλων των θλιμμένων». Στα αγγλικά Joy of All who Sorrow.). On the upper part, there is the Holy Trinity, the Christ and the God are sitted and the Holy Spirit is represented as a pigeon. In the corners,on the left and right, there is the sun and the moon.

Name: Icon with the Crucifixion of Christ and Saints
Description: In the center of the icon is the Crucifixion of Christ, above it - a bust of God Sabaoth, on the sides busts of the Mother of God and St. John the Theologian. In the four parts around the Crucifixion are: the Virgin of Kazan and a waist-length figure of St. Nicholas of Myra, the figures of archangel Michael and St. George on horses. The icon has an orange-red frame.
Current Location Name: Museum of the Bulgarian Revival and Constituent Assembly

Description: The martyred soldiers Boris and Gleb, born in Kyiv, sons of Prince Vladimir the Great (988-1015) is represented on one of the copper icons from the collection. They are depicted in semi-profile, on horseback, in military uniforms. Gleb is shown on the left, as a young man, with an oval face, with a small banner in his right hand. Boris is depicted on the right side, with his beard and wavy hair, with a sword that he wields menacingly with both hands. The horses are rendered in a parade-controlled movement, and the background is covered with vegetal motifs. The names of the saints are given in the upper part of the band of the composition: CTЬ ГЛБ / CTЬ БOPИC. At the top, the icon has a medallion fixed by casting on which the Holy Trinity is represented after the model of the painter Andrei Rubliov, the Old Testament Trinity.

The triptych is composed of three cast supports, joined together by two pairs of hinges. It
depicts a series of six saints with Desisis theme on the center. On the right panel, three saints are depicted standing and wearing ample vestments and circular nimbus. The first is Saint Philip, Metropolitan of Moscow (1507-1569), represented as an old man with a beard wearing a bishop's robes, richly decorated, and an episcopal hat, while he is holding the Scripture. Next to him, in a similar posture and clothes, is Saint Nicholas showing to the central panel. Saint Andrew (?) is depicted on the right side in a similar posture, in simple clothes, pointing the central panel with a Scripture. In the center, is placed  Jesus with his mother and Saint John the Baptist. They stay around Jesus who is seated on a richly decorated throne. The characters have circular nimbus and name inscriptions above head. On the right support is another group of three saints. The first one is the Saint Demetrios, in loose clothes, with wings, a sword in his right hand and an eight-edge cross in his left hand, which he raises towards Jesus. Behind him, are Saints Zosima and Savati of the Solovetky Monastery. They are depicted alike, with loose robes nimbus, while they have open palms facing the central panel.

Name: Saint Nicholas
Description: Canonic depictions of Saint Nicholas use the standard image of the Saint in bishop vestments, with the Virgin Mary and Jesus Christ. He is portrayed as an old man with a broad wrinkled forehead. Represented as a bust, the saint wears a large cloth. On his shoulders, he has a wide omophorion decorated with crosses. His right hand is bent over his chest and he holds two fingers raised as a sign of blessing, and with his left hand he holds an open book. On both sides of Nicholas’ head, in a small size, Jesus and His Mother appear in a semi-profile, blessing and offering gifts, a Holy Book and an omophorion, symbols of his ecclesiastical status. The background is decorated with vegetal motifs between which green and blue enamel was inserted.

Name: Triptych
Description:
The icon consists of four equal, rectangular panels with a trilobed pediment, fastened together with the help of three hinges. Each support contains five scenes related to the life of the Mother of God and Jesus Christ.
1. In the first panel, the scene in the pediment depicts the crucifixion of Jesus Christ with Mary, Longinus and an apostle. Crucifixion includes identifying elements: the 
suppedaneum, the cloth with the face of God, the angels descending, the spear and the sponge placed parallel to the cross, identification texts in Slavonic: INЦI / Сынъ Божіи / NI KA / М.Л.Р. At the bottom are four scenes from Virgin Mary’s life with well-defined borders which include  incised inscriptions in Russian. So the Annunciation appears in the upper left corner with the Virgin and an archangel Michael. The lower left scene completes the story with the episode of the birth of the Mother of God where Saints Joseph and Anne appear in an elaborate architectural setting,with columns and arches. The history of the Virgin's life is completed by the presentation at the temple on the lower right of the panel. The panel is completed by the scene of the birth of Jesus Christ placed in the upper right box. The composition is dominated by the bed on which Mary is seated and the groups of men and angels around them. 
2. The second panel is dominated by the figures of  God and Jesus Christ. They are placed around a cruciform globe with the Holy Spirit above. On the either side of this composition there are the symbols of the evangelists and two angels. In the top left register is the episode of the presentation of Jesus to the temple placed in an elaborate architectural setting. On the right side of the panel, appers the baptism of Jesus in which the composition is dominated by the figure of the Savior and John the Baptist next to the angels. In the
the lower left panel depicts the ascension scene of Jesus who is placed in a halo and on the ground are the apostles who kneel down Next to Jesus, two more saints appear. In the last register of this panel, the scene of Jesus Christ's entry to Jerusalem is rendered. He appears in the center of the composition riding a donkey.
3. The panel of the third begins with the scene of the appearance of Jesus Christ at the Sea of Tiberias, in which Jesus is depicted in a mandorla surrounded by seven apostles. In the upper right register, the ascension of Jesus is depicted. It dominates the composition in the superior register. In the lower part, there is a group of apostles with the Virgin Mary. In the lower register, on the left side, the descent of the Holy Spirit is render. In parallel with this scene, the episode of the Assumption of the Virgin Mary unfolds. The composition is dominated by the catafalque on which it is placed the body of Mary, around which the apostles are placed. In the upper part, Jesus Christ appears with a child in His arms symbolising His mother's soul. 
4. The fourth panel is dominated by the scene of the Virgin Mary in glory, where she is seated on a throne and is surrounded by a large group of saints. The four scenes that complete the panel depict the venerations of a four well-known icons: the Theotokos of Tikhvin, the Eleusis of Vladimir (Vladimirinskaia), the Virgin of Kazan and the Virgin
Mary of Novgorod. The icons are rendered centrally, flanked by saints and placed against the background of city profiles reminiscent of the home locations of icons. When closed, the four panels form a single structure decorated with the suppedaneum cross superimposed over the image of Jerusalem. The composition is framed in an oval space that is complemented with phytomorphic and architectural motifs.

Name: Crucifix
Description:
The crucifix has eight corners, in addition to the two arms we are used to, there are two more that are parallel to the horizontal one. Used extensively in the Old Believers’ communities, this type of cross is also called the Eastern or Russian cross. It has a vertical arm and three horizontal ones: a central one for the arms of Jesus, the upper one derived from the inscription INRI inserted by Pilate on the cross used to crucify Jesus Christ and in the lower part of the small structure a suppedaneum meant to support the legs of the Savior. 
At the top of the vertical arm of the crucifix a register is formed for the representation of God seen through the clouds, between two kneeling angels. The heavenly Father is depicted as an old man with long hair and beard, a halo around, dressed in a large coat, making the blessing gesture with his right hand, and on the left he usually holds a crucifix. Beneath Him is a small bird, a dove, a symbol of the Holy Spirit, which connects the Father with the crucified Son. Below the dove, it is an inscription in Russian: Ангели Господни (Angels of the Lord). On either side, on the arm, are two kneeling angels, with wings, loose garments, and haloes. Each holds a towel as a present. Under their feet is an inscription in Slavonic: Царь славы (The King of Glory). 
Jesus Christ occupies the central part of the cross where he is represented crucified in the way that it is well known. Above His head is an abbreviated inscription: I.N.Ц.И. (Iesus Nazarenus Rex Iudaeorum). This insertion of the scene of the crucifixion is accepted only by a fraction of the old Starover community.  The central part of the crucifix is dominated by the image of Jesus nailed to the cross, with his face still and his eyes closed, with his long hair and his beard carefully rendered. Around his head is a halo with the seal: Ο ὤ Ν ("The one who is"; Exodus 3: 13-14). The body is rendered at rest, weakened, with a cloth covering the hip area. Above the arms of Jesus there are two inscriptions: IC XC (Іисусъ Христосъ) and Сынъ Божіи (Son of God).  On either side of the cross on which Jesus is placed there are the personified figures of the sun and the moon, and their Russian names inscribed below, солнце (sun), respectively луна (moon). Another inscription is placed under the arms of the Savior. Along the body of Jesus are placed the Roman solders’ instruments of torture: the spear and the sponge. The spear is placed on the left side of Jesus and is marked with the Slavic letter K, the abbreviation of the word копие, and the sponge is placed on the right side and has next to it the letter T which takes the place of the word трость. 
Under Jesus’ feet there is a small oblique arm, called the suppedaneum, which is turned into an iconographic register where a part of Jerusalem is shown. The focus of the image is on the rooftops of defense buildings and landforms. The Savior has his feet nailed, and under them is another abbreviation М.Л.Р.Б (Место лобное рай бысть), a inscription that refers to the place where the skull of Adam was buried. This mention refers to the Christian tradition according to which Jesus was crucified on the place where the first man, Adam, was buried, so as the meaning expands and Jesus becomes the first man after the salvation of the world and the cross becomes the first tree of Paradise. The cross on which Jesus is placed is extended by the rendering of a cave in which the skull of Adam is outlined.

Name: Crucifix
Description: The bronze cross is set around the crucifixion of Jesus to which three more iconographic panels and a frieze of five seraphim (two of them are missing) have been added. On the top of the cross, there is a register with God seated in the middle, on a cloud, with open arms, a nimbus around the head. His face is erased as a result of intense use. A text in Russian is incised around His head: ГдЪC ѪЯѠФ (the abbreviation of "Gospod' Savaof" — Lord Savaot or Lord God of the Armies). Under the cloud, two angels with wings carry a cloth on their arms, placed right above the head of Jesus. Under each of them are letters of the abbreviation: Анг Гдни (Ангели Господни). The Holy Spirit is placed between them, with stretched wings, placed in a circular nimbus, with the abbreviation of his name: ДXЬ CT (meaning the Holy Spirit). Under the bird's feet, it lies a rectangular medallion with the initials: I.H.Ц.Н. (Jesus Nazarene Rex Iudaeorum). Right under it, there is Jesus Christ crucified. With the figure blunted due to adoration, the Savior is rendered according to the starovers’ norms: oversized palms, crucified nimbus, feet glued to the heels and fixed on the supraddaneum. Around the scene are are the initial of his name, IC XC, and a text around this side: PяпѩШiє ГДЯ NN_ГО ICЯ XPШЯ / КрестϪ ШвоемϪ Гокянѩѩќcѩв Влконитоевокрниє Швоеслявнмъ (in translation, "We kneel before this cross, Lord, and glorify the Holy Resurection”). The instruments of torture, the sponge and the lance, are place around the body as well as the Greek inscription divided into syllables: NI KA. The text is framed by a leaf.

Description: Panagia originates from the 19th century and belonged to Metropolitan Mitrofan Ban. It is encrusted with jewels, and the Nativity of Christ is represented in the central part.
